note: Five cognitive-design-architect variants, each pushed toward a different philosophy and required to answer the same nine hard problems. Seed material for the human's grilling decision, per PROCESS.md — not deciders.

proposals.name: THE ASSAY OFFICE
proposals.one_line: P1's instrument, turned around and pointed at 180 years of other people's counting machines — every number rides a named rail, every reading is stamped with who paid for it, and where the evidence refuses to answer, the instrument says NO READING.
proposals.philosophy:
P1's Instrument was a tool we held. P2 discovers that the tool is the subject. Thread 1 is not an aside — it is the finding: every pricing regime was created by a measurement regime, and the market's whole discipline was that somebody other than the seller did the counting. So the metaphor does not merely stretch; it turns reflexive. An assay office is the exact institutional form of that idea: a body that weighs and certifies metal precisely because neither buyer nor seller can be trusted to weigh it themselves. It is an instrument metaphor that is inherently about institutions and power, which is the stretch the brief demands.

Three cognitive commitments follow.

First, PROVENANCE GETS ITS OWN SPATIAL REGISTER. P2 has eight incompatible series, nineteen definitional seams and no continuous spine. If basis is encoded inside the chart — by hue, by tooltip — it competes with the value encoding and becomes a memory lookup. Moving it to a persistent sticky strip above the chart converts "which ruler is this?" from a recall task into a saccade. That is external cognition in Scaife and Rogers' sense: the display holds the state so working memory does not have to. Gestalt common region does the rest — a track is a region, and a gap in a track is a visible absence, which is far stronger than a missing point in a line, where absence is simply invisible.

Second, ENCODINGS MUST MATCH DATA TYPE, INCLUDING THE ABSENCE OF TYPE. Grade is ordinal, so it rides ordered channels (stroke weight, dash). Value is quantitative, so it rides position on a common scale — the top of Cleveland and McGill's accuracy ranking — which is also why stacked area is banned outright: every band above the baseline forces a length judgment against a moving reference, and the middle bands, where this story lives, are the worst case. And where three quantities are mutually unranked, no ordered channel may touch them at all. Vertical stacking is an ordered channel to a human reader; reading order and the near-universal sorted-bar convention guarantee an inferred ranking. So unranked data gets superposition on one axis with a lit ambiguity region, and the null gets a name.

Third, MOTION IS A PUNCTUATION MARK, NOT A TEXTURE. Motion is the most involuntary preattentive channel there is. At 160 marks, ambient jitter is a texture that says "alive." At 1,573 marks it is a field competing for the same orienting response — visual tinnitus, and a vestibular liability. So uncertainty is carried by geometry by default and by motion only when the reader asks. That is the honest place where the inherited device does not survive contact with the data, and saying so is part of the direction.
proposals.why_this_project:
Because this story's four chosen threads are all about who owns an instrument, and an instrument-shaped design is therefore not a metaphor laid on top — it is the argument's own shape.

Look at what the four threads actually are. Thread 1: who counted, and who paid the counter. Thread 2: the intermediary's cut, which ends as a number nobody can measure — two national advertiser associations tried and failed. Thread 3: who was allowed through the gate. Thread 4: who owns the front door and collects rent on it. Every one is a question about a measuring or gating apparatus and the interest of its owner. A design built as an assay office answers all four with one grammar: rails (whose scale), stamps (what grade), wedges (where two rulers disagree), and NO READING (where the instrument honestly returns nothing).

The heavy uncertainty is not an obstacle to this direction; it is its subject. 65 claims have an 80% CI wider than 60% of their central and must never be drawn as points. Era 1's four money-type shares sum to 62%. Era 7's three big pools are mutually unranked. The 2007-to-2025 fall from 2.0% to 1.32% of GDP is partly the ruler changing, worth 17.4% of level. A direction that treats uncertainty as a footnote would have to hide roughly a fifth of the record. This direction makes that fifth the most interesting part of the screen.

And the 180-year span is exactly the case where a chart system beats a chart. There is no continuous 1919–2026 by-medium series and there never will be — the brief's own FREEZE.md says the 2011–2025 gap cannot be improved without a licensed purchase. A design whose first move is to draw eight coverage tracks that visibly disagree about when the record even exists is telling the truth in its first two seconds, and it converts the project's biggest weakness into its opening exhibit.

Finally, the reflexive turn gives chapter 10 an ending that no other direction gets for free. The last exhibit in an assay office is the office's own scale, checked against the others. Chapter 10's verdict and handoff becomes the assay sheet: 63 cells, every grade chip visible, the thin places on show. The piece ends by measuring itself.

hard_problems.solution:
THE RAIL BOARD — a three-register chart system, not a chart, with a hard-coded splice ban.

Register A, THE RAIL BOARD (64px, sticky, always visible): eight horizontal tracks, one per series in adspend.json, sharing the hero x-axis 1840–2026. Each track draws a 5px band ONLY across the years that compiler actually published, terminating in a hard vertical buffer-stop cap — never a fade. Three textures carry three states: solid = published annual; discrete sleepers with no connecting band = benchmark-year-only (benchmarks_pre1919); 45-degree hatch in Paper Wash = constructed (bridge_mce_mg8, all grade C). Labels in IBM Plex Mono 10px at the left margin: COEN/MCE, MAGNA, IAB/PWC, IRS SOI, NAA, CENSUS, PRE-1919, BRIDGE (OURS). This one strip is simultaneously the legend, the provenance map, the coverage map and the gap map. It never scrolls away.

Register B, THE READING (~420px): the value chart. Default encoding is one line per rail, position on a common scale, NEVER stacked. Where two rails overlap in years, both draw and the vertical distance between them fills with a WEDGE — Paper Wash, hatched, directly labelled with the measured gap the dataset already carries in concordance.magnitude. The Coen/MAGNA wedge at 1980 is annotated in reader-facing prose: '1980 is the only year both counted. They are 23.4% apart. Most of that gap — about 69% — is which things got counted. Only 7.2 points is the price basis.' The wedge is not an apology; it is the exhibit.

For composition (27 medium labels, money-type splits) Register B switches to THE SMALL-MULTIPLE BANK: 8–11 panels on a shared y-scale, each medium on its own aligned baseline, total as the first and largest panel. Parts-to-whole is bought back with a single-year CROSS-SECTION BAR — a stacked bar is legitimate for one column read as one column, and illegitimate as a time series.

Register C, THE SHARE RULE (~120px): ad spend as a share of GDP, 1867–2025, the chapter-09 spine, with every basis change drawn as a labelled vertical seam.

Fourth mode, THE RAIL DIFFERENCE: hold two rails and Register B flips to plot their ratio across the overlap. Coen over IAB internet goes 0.662 (1997) to 0.805 (2000) to 0.497 (2007). That is a chart of two instruments diverging, and it is the single most P2-native chart in the system.

The splice ban is an invariant, not a style: the path builder refuses to connect two points whose source_series differ. `if (a.source_series !== b.source_series) breakPath()`. The 2008–2020 hole draws as a hole — Coen stops at 2007 with a buffer stop, MAGNA resumes 17.4% lower on the restated basis, and the bridge wedge between them is hatched with its own $211bn–$244bn thickness. The phantom collapse is thereby shown to BE a phantom.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale: Three principles, each doing specific work. (1) Cleveland and McGill's encoding hierarchy puts position-on-a-common-scale first and area/length-on-a-shifting-baseline far below; stacked area and streamgraph force exactly the inferior judgment, and force it worst on the middle bands, which is where the medium mix story lives. Small multiples restore a common baseline to every member at the cost of the summation reading, which the cross-section bar returns as a separate, correctly-shaped task. (2) Ware's channel-orthogonality: value and provenance must not compete for the same channel or the reader must serialize two questions. Giving provenance its own spatial register with its own texture channel makes both answerable in one fixation. (3) Gestalt figure-ground and common region turn absence into content — a terminated track with a buffer stop is a perceived object, whereas a line that simply stops is perceived as an ending, and a line that is silently spliced is perceived as continuity that never existed. Naming and measuring the wedge also defuses the anchoring risk: a reader who sees a labelled 23.4% gap cannot anchor on a single spliced trajectory, because there is no single trajectory to anchor on.

hard_problems.solution:
THE SLEEPER FIELD, plus a different hero visual for era 1 entirely.

On the spine: era 1 renders on the same x-axis and the same y-scale as everything else, but as sleepers, not track. Each benchmark year (1867, 1880, 1890, 1900, 1914, 1918) draws as a vertical CI BAR with serif caps — the full 80% interval, no central dot, because these are exactly the marks the rigor rule forbids as points. 1867 is $50m on [30, 80]; that bar is nearly three times as tall as it is wide and it sits in the emptiest region of the screen. Between the sleepers: nothing. A faint dotted rule spans 1840–1918 labelled, in plain reader-facing English, 'No year-by-year record exists for these 77 years.' Where two vintages disagree (1900–1918, by 9–20%), two sleepers draw at the same year, offset 3px, so the compilers' disagreement is a visible doubling rather than a footnote.

Off the spine: era 1's chapter does NOT use the money chart as its hero. Its real subject is a price with no count, so its hero is THE COMMISSION SPREAD — one quantity across 77 years, drawn as an interval that collapses. It opens as a band from 10% to 50% (agents took anything, nobody could check anybody), narrows to a hard 15% line by the early 1890s, and gets a lock mark at 1893 when publishers agreed to pay commission only to recognised agents. One mark, one era, honest about having no annual money series.

Structurally, the six benchmarks become the era's SCROLL STATIONS — one beat per benchmark, the field accumulating sleepers as the reader descends. By the end of era 1 the reader has watched six wide intervals arrive and has learned the CI-bar grammar on the sparsest data in the project.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale: A timeline sets a strong schema expectation of continuity; violating it silently is the classic integrity failure, because the reader's perceptual system will interpolate. Rendering the 77-year gap as labelled negative space uses figure-ground reversal to make the absence the figure — the emptiest region of the chart becomes the most annotated. Teaching the interval grammar HERE rather than in a data-rich era is a deliberate sequencing choice from worked-example research: introduce a new representation on the instance where its necessity is unmissable, so that later, denser uses are recognized rather than decoded. And giving era 1 a separate hero avoids the standard failure mode where a data-poor period is forced into a data-rich chart form and therefore reads as flat and uninteresting — a framing artifact, not a fact about 1840.

hard_problems.solution:
THE ASSAY MARK — a static three-part grammar as the default, with jitter demoted to a triggered reveal named TREMOR.

Honest verdict first: ambient measurement jitter does NOT survive contact with 1,573 points, and I am not going to pretend it does. Three failures. It captures involuntary attention indiscriminately at high set size — 1,573 competing motion signals is not texture, it is noise. It encodes CI width as amplitude, a magnitude judgment on a moving target, which is near the bottom of the accuracy ranking and cannot resolve the 65 wide-CI claims from the rest. And the vestibular cost scales with the animated area, so a full-field shimmer is a motion-sickness surface, not an accent.

So the default is geometry:

GRADE rides stroke weight and terminal — an ordered channel for an ordinal variable. Grade A: 1.5px, hard square cap, reads as stamped. Grade B: 1.25px, round cap. Grade C: 1px and the outline turns dashed (3-2). No hue is spent on grade at all.

CI rides the mark's actual geometry, by an arithmetic rule printed in the legend as the rule itself. ciWidth/central > 0.6 draws as an interval bar with NO central tick — that is the brief's 65 claims, implemented as a rendering branch, not a guideline. Between 0.2 and 0.6, interval bar WITH a central tick. Below 0.2, a point with whiskers. Three visual species, one arithmetic boundary, so a reader can reverse-engineer the rule from the picture.

WHO PAID rides a 3px underline swatch beneath the mark's label in tooltips and in thread visuals — amber for the seller's own number, cyan for an independent one. This is P2's addition to P1's grammar and it is the thesis in a channel.

TREMOR is the survivor. Triggered on hover or keyboard focus, it makes that mark and its claim-family siblings vibrate within their own intervals — amplitude 0.15 x CI width, capped at 6px, 7Hz, 1.2s, decaying into a SETTLE tail. And it fires once at full field, in chapter 01: all 1,573 marks tremble for 1.6s and settle, under the line 'Move the ruler and the number moves. Every number here was made by somebody.' The emotional payload P1 got from ambient shimmer is spent once, at maximum effect, and never taxes the reader again.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale: Motion pops out preattentively and involuntarily regardless of set size — which is precisely why it fails as an ambient encoding at n=1,573: pop-out only helps when few items have the feature, and here most of the field would carry it. Converting motion to a demand-driven reveal restores its selectivity: when one mark trembles among 1,572 still ones, the pop-out works exactly as intended. Meanwhile stroke weight and dash are ordered visual variables in Bertin's sense and match grade's ordinal type, so no arbitrary mapping has to be memorized. Making the CI-to-geometry rule arithmetic and printing it converts a design decision into a learnable inference rule — the reader stops asking 'why is this one a bar?' after about the fourth instance. Reserving one full-field motion event also respects the one-change-per-beat rule from narrative visualization: the single most expensive perceptual event in the project is spent teaching the grammar, not decorating a chapter.

hard_problems.solution:
THE RECLASSIFICATION SLIDE — object constancy on the exact block that moves, with the interval visibly changing SHAPE rather than position.

The data makes this buildable and precise. The mover is one identifiable block: local Yellow Pages, 2000, $11,135m, 4.4995 percentage points of the 2000 US total. Under the geographic rule, local_retail is 28.32% on [20.8, 33.0] and direct_response 24.71%. Under the unified-intent rule, local_retail is 23.82% on [20.8, 28.5] and direct_response 29.21%. The interval NARROWS from 12.2pp to 7.70pp — the ceiling falls by the whole block, the floor holds at 20.8 — because 4.50pp of the native downside WAS the directory convention.

Draw the 2000 market as four columns of unit particles, one particle = $1bn, roughly 247 particles total, countable in gestalt clusters. The eleven Yellow Pages particles are visually distinct from first appearance — same fill as their host pool, plus a persistent 1px outline. They are never anonymous, so they can never be lost.

The control is a two-position switch labelled with the RULE, never the answer: 'Split directory money by who bought it' / 'Put all directory money in one pool.' Flip it and the eleven particles physically travel, RECLASSIFY verb, 700ms, staggered nearest-first so they read as a body moving rather than a swarm.

Three annotated things happen at once. (1) The two columns swap order. (2) The local pool's CI bracket does not translate — its top edge descends 4.5pp while its bottom edge stays pinned at 20.8, with a live readout 'range 12.2 points to 7.7 points.' (3) A horizontal overlap band stays LIT under both states, labelled 'These two still overlap. Neither rule tells us which is bigger.'

Both states get equal visual weight — no default-is-truth styling. One persistent line notes the project's stated convention: 'Comparisons across eras use the second rule.' Hiding that would be its own dishonesty.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale: This is a change-blindness problem before it is anything else. Two static charts side by side, or a cross-fade, produce a 'different chart' percept, and Rensink's work says the reader will fail to localize what changed even while confidently reporting that something did. Animated object constancy with preserved identity forces the visual system to track the same objects through the transformation, which is what converts 'the answer changed' into 'I moved that money' — the transformation IS the lesson, so the transformation must be the animation. Labelling the control with the rule rather than the outcome is a framing guard: a control labelled 'correct view' would anchor the reader on one answer, and framing effects on a genuinely underdetermined choice are exactly the bias to avoid. The interval-shape change is the deepest teaching moment in the whole rigor layer, because it demonstrates something readers almost never see — that part of a confidence interval can be uncertainty ABOUT THE CLASSIFICATION, and settling the classification by rule removes it. Pinning the floor while dropping the ceiling makes that decomposable by eye.

hard_problems.solution:
THE UNRANKED FIELD, and a first-class typographic state called NO READING.

Era 7's four pools: national_brand [25, 47], local_retail [15, 31], classified [1.4, 6.8], direct_response [29.5, 47]. Classified is ordered below all three. The other three are mutually unranked, and brand and response sit 1.4 points apart on centrals.

The rule I hold to: no ordered channel may touch unordered data. That rules out bars, stacks and lists — but it ALSO rules out three interval bars stacked in three rows, because vertical position plus reading order plus the sorted-bar convention produce an inferred ranking no disclaimer can undo.

So: remove the vertical dimension. The three unranked pools draw as three interval bars on the SAME horizontal line, superposed, each at 45% opacity, on a shared 0–50% share axis. They are distinguished by hue and by direct labels placed at their centrals with short leader lines. The region where all three overlap is filled with cross-hatch and labelled once, in plain English: 'Any of these three could be the largest.' Classified sits on a separate row BELOW a hairline rule, because it genuinely is ordered against them — and that hairline is a visual assertion that the evidence supports a rank here and not above it.

Interaction, one gesture, and it is the honest counter to a reader who suspects coyness: a confidence handle drags the intervals from 80% down toward 50%. All three narrow together — and at 50% they still overlap. You cannot buy a ranking with a looser confidence level. The reader proves this to themselves in two seconds.

The numeric readout never prints a sorted list. It prints 'Largest: no answer. Smallest: classified.'

NO READING is then promoted to a system-wide state, set in Martian Mono, Zinc, small caps: `NO READING — RANGES OVERLAP`, with a plain-language line beneath it. It appears in three places: here, at era 1's 38% unassigned residual, and at thread 2's era-7 column that cannot be closed. Making the null a styled, named, repeated element is what stops it reading as a bug or an oversight.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale: Munzner's expressiveness principle states it cleanly: the visual encoding must express all and only the information in the data. An ordered spatial channel expresses an ordering the evidence does not contain, so it is not merely suboptimal — it is false. Vertical stacking is unavoidably ordered to a human reader because two independent conventions reinforce it: top-to-bottom reading order, and the overwhelming prior that ranked charts are sorted. Superposition on a single common-scale axis expresses exactly what is known — each pool's plausible range — and nothing more. The cross-hatched ambiguity region gives the null a positive perceptual form rather than leaving it as an inference the reader must construct, which matters because absent evidence is systematically underweighted. The confidence handle is doing worked-example work: it converts an abstract statistical claim ('these are unranked') into a manipulable demonstration whose result is invariant under the reader's own attempts to break it, which is far more convincing than any assertion.

hard_problems.solution:
THE BENCH — one apparatus, twenty-one presets, three fixed zones, controls unlocked progressively.

The governing decision: 21 scenarios are settings of ONE constant apparatus, never 21 charts. The schema is built once and reused twenty-one times.

ZONE 1, THE SLATE (left, ~240px): bidder cards. Each carries a name, a bid handle, a predicted-CTR handle, and a true-CTR handle drawn BEHIND the predicted one so a mismatch shows as a gap — filled with the same hatch used for rail wedges, so the grammar unifies: a wedge always means two rulers disagree. That gap is where the seller's own estimate lives.

ZONE 2, THE PAGE (centre, ~320px): two slots as actual rectangles, the second drawn at 40% the height of the first so the position multiplier is SEEN, not stated. A physical switch above: RANK BY BID / RANK BY BID x CLICK RATE / RANK BY BID x CLICK RATE^γ. Flipping it makes ad cards fly between slots with object constancy — same card, same colour, moving. That is sc-01 and sc-02 in one gesture: 'Cedar bids a third of what Aster bids, and gets clicked five times as often.'

ZONE 3, THE TILL (right, ~280px): three readouts, always the same three, always in the same place, Martian Mono tabular: REVENUE PER 1,000 SHOWINGS / CLICKS DELIVERED / AVERAGE PRICE PER CLICK. Each shows its value plus a ghost of the previous state with a signed delta. This is where 'the sign everyone gets backwards' becomes unmissable: +86.6% revenue, +222% clicks, MINUS 42% price per click, three aligned arrows, two up and one down, in one glance.

THE BAND (sc-05, the hardest lesson): the REVENUE readout is never a number alone. From sc-04 onward it is a marker sitting inside a horizontal band spanning $440 to $760. The reader drags a bidder's bid and watches revenue slide inside the band with their own hand — proving the seller's take is chosen by the bidders, not by the rule. Then sc-10 overlays rGSP's +5.74% as a tiny arrow inside that same band, covering 7.9% of a band the mechanism itself leaves 73% wide. That single frame is the most devastating in the piece.

BIDDER MODE is a three-position switch: TRUTHFUL / SHADED (equilibrium) / YOUR HAND. In YOUR HAND the top readout swaps to VALE'S PROFIT and the reader drags from 10 down through 5, watching $400 become $640 — its own payoff, not the seller's. That is sc-04, and the swap of what the till reports is deliberate: the lesson is about whose interest is being served.

sc-06 is a TWIN BENCH — the apparatus duplicates, left GSP, right first-price-with-shading, both driven by one slate. The two revenue numbers are identical for every n, and the reader steps n and watches them move together. Identical values in mirrored positions is a symmetry judgment, which humans read far better than they compare two numbers in prose.

sc-08 uses a deliberate freeze: one bidder, one reserve dial, $0.01 to $1.00, revenue $0.40 to $40. The PAGE zone visibly does not animate at all — same ad, same user, same slot — while the till goes 100x. Absence of change in one region beside 100x change in another IS the exhibit.

GUARD AGAINST TEACHING A DEAD MECHANISM: a permanent ERA STAMP sits in the bench's top-left corner in mono — `ERA 6 · 2002–2008 · SEARCH`, or `ERA 7 · 2019– · DISPLAY: FIRST PRICE`, or `ERA 7 · 2019– · SEARCH: rGSP`. It is chrome, not a caption, and it changes with every preset. sc-10 puts two stamps on two benches: same year, opposite directions, display went first-price and search never did.

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE against 40 variables: the bench opens with three live controls. + predicted-vs-true CTR unlocks at sc-07, + reserve at sc-08, + γ at sc-09, + pricing rule at sc-06. Never more than five live controls at once.

NAVIGATION: a numbered strip along the bottom — ten C-stops in one row, eleven D-stops in a second, greyed until their chapter unlocks. Any scenario is one click from any other. The D-series is honestly a DIFFERENT apparatus — THE LEDGER, a two-column flow of revenue in and payments out, with the equity leg on a stepped axis carrying a labelled break, because D3's warrant went from $13.871m carried to $1,134.6m realised and a smooth log axis would hide the shock that IS the finding.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale: Sweller's worked-example and split-attention findings drive the whole structure. A constant apparatus lets the reader build one schema and then vary parameters within it; twenty-one distinct charts would force twenty-one schema constructions and burn the entire intrinsic-load budget on layout rather than mechanism. Fixed spatial zones mean the reader never re-searches for the answer — the till is always right there, so the read is a fixation, not a scan. Progressive control disclosure respects the roughly four-chunk working-memory limit for simultaneously manipulable variables; exposing forty at once guarantees abandonment, and Hick's law makes even the choice among them costly. The signed-delta ghost turns the C2/C3 lesson into a preattentive pop-out: two arrows point up and one points down, and the contradictory direction is detected before it is read. The band is the key epistemic device — a single number invites the reader to treat mechanism revenue as a fact, whereas a marker the reader themselves slides inside a band teaches that the quantity is chosen, not determined. And the permanent era stamp exists because over-generalization is the predictable failure of any teaching simulator: without a persistent scope marker readers will export 'auctions are second-price' as a current fact, which the record specifically refutes for display after 2019.

hard_problems.solution:
THE ERA CARD plus THE FIELD RAIL — a repeating scaffold and a transpose, so cross-era comparison costs zero scrolling.

Per-era scaffold: every era chapter opens with an identical ERA CARD — a fixed 3x3 grid of the nine fields (creators, buyers, sellers, medium, scale, pricing, measurement, targeting, events), in the same nine positions in all seven eras. Each cell carries three things: the field name in Martian Mono small caps; the era's one-sentence answer in Newsreader; and a GRADE CHIP STRIP — the thread-candidate notation like `1A3B0C` rendered as three tiny stacked bars, so the evidence profile of that field in that era is readable without reading. By era 3 the reader knows where PRICING lives without looking, because it has been in the same position three times.

Cross-era comparison without scrolling twice: THE FIELD RAIL. Click any field name on any era card and the page transposes — the 3x3 grid morphs into a single-field, seven-era strip, one row, seven columns, era 1 through era 7, showing that field's answer in all seven eras at once. The cell you clicked stays anchored in place and the other six fly in around it, RECLASSIFY verb, ~500ms. Click again to return. The reader never leaves their scroll position. Comparing era 3's PRICING to era 6's is one click and one fixation.

The complete 9 x 7 = 63-cell matrix appears exactly once, in chapter 10, as THE ASSAY SHEET — one screen, reduced type, all sixty-three cells present. But it ships in a different encoding for a different task: the assay sheet shows GRADE CHIPS ONLY, not sentences. Sixty-three sentences is far beyond a reading task; sixty-three chips is a pattern-detection task, and the pattern is the point — where is the evidence thin? Era 1's measurement column and era 7's money-type row will be visibly pale. That is the project measuring itself, which is the honest ending an assay office earns.

Mobile inverts the priority: a 3x3 grid at 360px is nine stacked cards, so the transpose becomes the PRIMARY interaction and the field rail becomes a horizontal swipe through eras with snap points.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale: Consistency of spatial position across seven repetitions builds a spatial index in long-term memory, which is why the ninth cell of era 6 costs almost nothing to find after six prior cards — this is the same mechanism that makes familiar interfaces feel fast, and it is cheaper than any labelling improvement. The transpose is Shneiderman's overview-then-zoom applied to a matrix, but its real virtue is that it eliminates the working-memory carry: comparing two cells by scrolling requires holding cell A in memory while locating cell B, and the answer degrades with scroll distance. Co-location makes it a perceptual comparison instead of a mnemonic one. Shipping the 63-cell matrix in a chips-only encoding is task-encoding alignment: sentences serve a reading task and are correct on the era card; chips serve a pattern-detection task and are correct on the assay sheet. Using one encoding for both would fail one of them.

hard_problems.solution:
TWO DIFFERENT RESPONSIVE PROBLEMS, TWO DIFFERENT ANSWERS — and a named amputation list.

Governing rule, stated first and defended hardest: NO FINDING IS REACHABLE ONLY BY INTERACTION. Every interactive has a scripted fallback — a scroll-driven sequence through three to five of its own states with the annotation baked in. A reader who never touches anything still gets the whole argument. Interaction adds exploration; it never adds information. This is simultaneously the mobile answer, the accessibility answer and the screenshot answer.

HERO CHART ON MOBILE. The rail board SURVIVES intact — it is a thin strip, it works at 360px, and it is the honesty layer, so it is the last thing that may ever be dropped. Register B becomes ONE RAIL AT A TIME with a horizontal swipe between rails; the wedge becomes an explicit 'compare' state rather than a default. This is not a downgrade: two overlapping ribbons at 360px are illegible, and animating the SETTLE from one rail to the other while the wedge paints in actually teaches the gap better than superposition, because the reader sees the movement. Register C drops out of the sticky and becomes an inline figure. The small-multiple bank becomes a two-column grid plus a snap-point filmstrip, one panel per screen, for the annotated beats.

BENCH ON MOBILE — deliberately dropped, and why. (1) Free-drag on bid handles: gone, replaced by stepper buttons and four preset bid values, because a 44px drag target with its readout elsewhere on screen is a failed interaction — the finger occludes the number. (2) The twin bench for sc-06: gone, replaced by a flip toggle where the revenue readout STAYS PINNED IN PLACE while everything else changes. Identity proven by non-movement of the number is actually a stronger proof than side-by-side, and it works at any width. (3) The 21-stop strip: gone, replaced by a prev/next pager scoped to the current chapter's two-to-four scenarios, plus a 'see all' sheet. (4) The D-series dual axis: gone entirely, replaced by two sequential single-axis panels with scroll-linked reveal. (5) γ and format multiplier: hidden behind an 'advanced' disclosure, present but not primary.

ADDED for mobile, not merely preserved: the TILL relocates from a right column to a sticky bottom bar, three readouts in one row, thumb-adjacent and never occluded. On desktop the readout belongs near the gaze path; on mobile it belongs near the thumb. That is a genuine re-layout, not a stack.

Also mobile-specific: the P7 transpose becomes primary rather than secondary, and the P5 unranked field rotates so the share axis runs vertically — the one place where a vertical axis is safe, because all three bars share it and none is above another.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale: Fitts's law makes the drag-handle decision for us: on a touch surface the target is the finger's contact patch, roughly 9mm, and precise value setting through a 9mm aperture with the feedback rendered outside the occlusion zone is not a usability weakness but a failure. Steppers convert a continuous positioning task into a discrete selection task, which is exactly the right trade when the teaching point is the direction of change rather than its precise magnitude. Pinning the revenue readout for sc-06 exploits change detection in reverse — the visual system is highly sensitive to onset and motion, so a value that conspicuously does NOT move while its surroundings do is registered as an event, which is precisely the claim ('first price pays the seller identically'). And the no-finding-behind-interaction rule follows from the plain fact that most readers do not interact: designing the argument to depend on a gesture means designing it to be missed. The scripted fallback is the primary path with interaction layered on, not the reverse.

hard_problems.solution:
FOUR VISUALS. I accept thread 1's two-track timeline but change its colour encoding from nominal to ordered, which is what makes it work without a legend.

THREAD 1 — THE COUNTER'S LEDGER. Two tracks on the hero x-axis, 1840–2026. Top: the counting institution as a labelled bar (Rowell's directory 1869; ABC 1914; CAB 1930; Hooper 1934; Nielsen buys Hooper 1950; BRC 1964; people meters 1987; DART's log 1996; Quality Score 2002; nobody, 2010s). Bottom: its funder, same x-extent. THE CRITICAL CHANGE: the funder colour is not seven arbitrary hues on a legend. It is a single ORDERED ramp on one dimension — distance from the seller. Amber at the seller end, Verdigris for tripartite and industry in the middle, Cyan at the advertiser and rival-medium end, each with a redundant texture for colourblind safety. Because the thread's whole claim is that somebody other than the seller counted, and that the rule broke around 1996, the encoding delivers the thesis preattentively: the bottom track goes amber after 1996 and STAYS amber. The reader sees the finding before reading a word. The two price shocks get vertical shock lines with the 1987 interactive (below) and the 2021 undercount drawn as a $468M block against that year's national revenue.

THREAD 2 — THE DOLLAR, SEVEN TIMES. Seven vertical unit columns, one per era, 100 particles each = $100 of the advertiser's gross outlay, under a declared convention printed on the visual. Because the thread's own hole is that these are NOT one quantity — the denominators differ — two honesty devices are structural. Any era where the convention does not hold gets a hatched 'not on this basis' block, never a smoothed number: era 1's stack is incomplete because national reps' rates are unknown. Era 3's rep-firm range (5–20%) draws its partition boundary as a fifteen-particle gradient rather than a hard edge, because the boundary genuinely is a range. And era 7's column CANNOT BE CLOSED: 51% reaches the publisher, 15% is unattributable, and those fifteen particles hover unplaced in a visible hole. A 180-year story about transparency ends in a column with a hole in it, and you can see the exact particles nobody can account for. A second small panel kills a legend with grade-A data: commissions actually received, 14.13 / 13.92 / 14.16 / 13.18 / 10.98% for 1977–1997 — four flat dots then a step, which instantly refutes 'the commission died in the 1980s.'

THREAD 3 — THE GATE. Two panels that must not be joined, separated by a full-height gutter that IS the prohibition. Left: classified and directory DOLLAR SHARE, eras 1–4, sitting stubbornly at 3–13%, linear axis. Right: advertiser HEAD COUNT, 3,800 to 53,000 to 80,000 to ~1M to >10M, log axis, with grade-C intervals as bands — Google's 550k-to-2.6M band should look as huge as it is. The gutter carries, as a visible physical object rather than a footnote, 'Two different measures. Do not read across.' Inside the gutter sits the GATE CARD STACK, one card per era with four rows: deposit, minimum spend, review, approval time. The era-6 card is the A-grade exhibit and gets two columns — Overture (10c minimum bid, $20 a month, human review) beside AdWords ($5 once, no minimum, automatic) — same year, same market. That card is the most typographically confident object in the project, because it is the cleanest causal exhibit in the whole record.

THREAD 4 — THE DOOR TOLL. Small multiples, seven panels, one per era, each showing the payout as a share of the revenue it generated (27% to 5–20% to 56% to 85% to 36%) on an IDENTICAL 0–100% scale, so shares compare at a glance. Beneath them, one absolute-dollar strip on its own axis with an explicit marked break, because $26.3bn in 2021 against 1938's affiliate compensation spans four orders of magnitude and a smooth log would flatten the shock that is the finding. Eras 1, 3 and 4 are structural analogies with one or two numbers each, so their panels draw at reduced opacity inside dashed frames labelled STRUCTURAL, NOT MEASURED — the grid stays complete so the 180-year continuity reads, but the thin panels announce themselves. The AOL warrant gets an inset: $13.871m carried against $1,134.6m realised, bars drawn to true scale so the first is a 1.2% sliver, and the sliver IS the argument. Closing frame: the 2021 toll bar holds its position while a line lands — 'The 2025 ruling banned exclusive deals. It did not stop the payments.'
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale: Thread 1's change from nominal hue to an ordered ramp is the single highest-leverage decision in the four. Seven arbitrary categorical colours force a legend lookup per bar — a serial memory task repeated across 180 years of timeline. An ordered ramp on 'distance from the seller' makes the categories a scale, and scales are read preattentively as a gradient, so the 1996 break becomes a colour flood detected in the first fixation. It also means the encoding cannot be read except in the terms of the thesis, which is legitimate here precisely because the thesis IS about seller-distance. Thread 2 uses unit visualization because the claim is compositional and countable, and because a hole in a column of countable objects is a categorically stronger percept than a missing wedge in a bar — absence of an expected object is detected, whereas a shorter bar is merely a smaller quantity. Thread 3 uses common region: a visible gutter is a Gestalt separator, and separating two incommensurable measures physically is far more reliable than warning against comparing them, because the warning is processed after the comparison has already happened. Thread 4 uses small multiples for the shares — Tufte's within-the-eyespan comparison on a common scale, no memory carry — but refuses a log axis for the absolute strip, because logs are the standard way to make a four-order-of-magnitude finding look ordinary, and the shock here is the content.

proposals.type:
All three P1 faces inherited, with one face given a second job and no fourth face added.

MARTIAN MONO — display and numerals, as in P1, plus a new role: it is the ASSAY FACE. Anything that is provenance or metadata is Martian Mono — rail names, grade chips, era stamps on the bench, the NO READING state, the era-card field names in small caps, the chapter progress bar. The reader learns one rule in the first screen and never re-learns it: mono is the machine talking about the evidence; serif is the argument. All number columns set with tabular figures, and the 63-cell assay sheet at 11px, where the chips must stay legible.

NEWSREADER — body prose, as in P1, and there is a lot more of it: ten chapters plus four thread chapters. It also carries the sentence content of era cards and every reader-facing annotation, which means every string in Newsreader must clear the four readability gates. Headline scale 64px/1.05; body 19px/1.62 at a 68-character measure; annotations 15px/1.45.

IBM PLEX MONO — data chrome, as in P1: tooltips, CI values, A/B/C grades, axis tick labels, rail track labels at 10px. Kept distinct from Martian Mono so the hierarchy has two mono weights — Martian for assertions the design makes, Plex for values the data reports.

No fourth face. P2's tabular pressure (era cards, gate cards, assay sheet) is real, but it is solved by tabular figures and by the mono/serif split, not by adding a typeface. Adding one would be decoration, which is the exact failure mode this direction has to avoid.

proposals.motion:
Five verbs. Two inherited, three new, each earning its place. Motion budget: at most one animated region on screen at any time, and one change per scroll beat — highlight OR annotate, never both.

SETTLE (inherited) — critically damped ease-out, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), 600–900ms. Any value arriving at a measured position. A galvanometer needle.

SWEEP (inherited) — near-linear, ~1400ms per century of x-axis, for rails drawing left to right. P2 adds one rule: a rail sweeps only across the years it actually covers and STOPS DEAD at its buffer stop, with no ease-out. The abrupt stop is the content.

TREMOR (new; replaces P1's ambient jitter) — triggered, never ambient. Amplitude 0.15 x the mark's own CI width, hard-capped at 6px, 7Hz, 1.2s, decaying into a SETTLE tail. Fires on hover or keyboard focus of a mark and its claim-family siblings. Fires once at full field, in chapter 01, for 1.6s. That is the entire motion budget for uncertainty in the project.

RECLASSIFY (new) — the object-constancy particle move. 700ms, SETTLE easing, staggered 6ms per particle ordered by distance travelled, nearest first, so a moving block reads as a body rather than a swarm. Used for era 5's eleven Yellow Pages particles, for ad cards moving between auction slots, and for the era-card transpose.

STAMP (new) — 140ms scale from 1.06 to 1.00, no bounce, no overshoot. Fires on grade chips and on the bench's era stamp when a preset loads. It is the only fast motion in the system, so it reads as punctuation: an assertion being made.

PREFERS-REDUCED-MOTION — a complete alternative, not a shrug.
· TREMOR is replaced by a permanently drawn hatched CI band at every mark, so uncertainty moves entirely into geometry, plus numeric CI in the tooltip. Nothing is lost; the encoding simply becomes static.
· RECLASSIFY becomes a 200ms cross-fade PLUS a mandatory ghost outline of the block's previous position, held for 3s. This is non-negotiable: a cross-fade alone destroys object constancy and would delete the entire P4 lesson for reduced-motion readers. The ghost outline is how they get it back.
· SWEEP renders complete on scroll-in, with buffer-stop caps thickened to 2px so terminations stay emphatic.
· SETTLE becomes instant positioning.
· STAMP becomes a 100ms opacity fade.
· The chapter-01 full-field TREMOR becomes a single static frame showing every mark's CI band, under the identical caption.
· The bench: all transitions instant, but the till's ghost-previous-value and signed deltas remain, because they are static typography — the entire C2/C3 sign lesson survives untouched.
proposals.signature_interaction:
THE INSTRUMENT SWAP — 1987, the people meters.

A full-width scene, two panels and one switch. Left: a grid of 1,200 dots, one per metered home in the national panel — the same dots the reader has already met in era 3 and era 4, so they carry identity across chapters. Right: THE TILL, in Martian Mono, four readouts stacked — MEASURED PRIME-TIME AUDIENCE, CBS, ABC, PRICE PER THOUSAND.

Between them, one physical switch, two positions, labelled with the instrument and not the answer: DIARY + METER / PEOPLE METER.

The reader flips it. And the design is the STILLNESS: not one of the 1,200 dots moves. Not one. Nothing about America's television watching changes, because nothing about America's television watching did change. Meanwhile the right panel drops — measured prime-time audience minus 10%, CBS minus 13%, ABC minus 13% — and the price follows the measurement down, with make-goods owed in scatter worth more than the upfront that had been sold.

Then one line lands in Newsreader, alone: "Nobody watched less television. The ruler changed."

Two things make this the signature rather than a scene. First, it is the thesis in a gesture a child can perform, on grade-A and grade-B evidence, with the emotional payload carried by an absence of motion rather than a presence of it — which is why it survives reduced-motion mode completely intact.

Second, it becomes a LEARNED OPERATOR. The same switch chrome, the same two-panel stillness, returns twice: at the 2021 Nielsen undercount, where the same gesture produces at least $468M of lost national ad revenue with the audience unchanged; and at the 2019 rGSP frame, where flipping the mechanism raises top-slot prices 5.91% with no opt-out and nothing visible changing on the page. By the third use the reader recognises the gesture before reading the label and knows what it means: change the instrument, hold the world still, watch the money move. A repeated gesture with a constant meaning is the strongest thing an interactive essay can leave in someone's memory a week later — and here it happens to be the argument.
proposals.what_it_sacrifices:
Seven honest costs.

1. FIRST-CONTACT GRIP. A rail board and a field of measurements is a cool opening. A direction that led with "Google is paid $26.3 billion a year to be the default" would grip harder in three seconds and share better. I am trading immediate punch for a reading grammar that pays off across fourteen units of content. For a casual social-referral reader, this direction loses.

2. A MONOTONE OF CAVEAT. Because every chapter re-runs the same honesty grammar — rails, wedges, intervals, NO READING — the piece risks a flat epistemic register. P1 could afford this over seven beats; P2 has ten chapters plus four thread chapters. The thread visuals are deliberately more expressive to counteract it, but the risk is real, and the prose will have to carry more of the narrative rise than P1's did.

3. PERMANENT SCREEN COST FOR METADATA. 64px of sticky rail board on every frame is real estate a single-hero direction spends on the chart. On a 667px phone that is roughly a tenth of the viewport permanently allocated to provenance. I judge it worth it because seams are content — but a direction that put basis in a tooltip would ship a bigger chart.

4. THE BENCH IS 35–45% OF THE BUILD FOR ONE CHAPTER AND A CODA. Twenty-one presets, five progressive unlocks, a twin mode, a separate ledger apparatus for the D-series, and a mobile amputation. A direction that made the auction a sequence of annotated static frames would ship in half the time and lose maybe a quarter of the teaching. I choose the bench because sc-05's band cannot be taught statically — the reader has to slide revenue inside it with their own hand — but it is the single largest schedule risk in the project and should be scoped as such.

5. DELIBERATELY THIN COLOUR CAPACITY. Eight tokens, two of them carrying the entire thesis, means the 27 medium labels can never be distinguished by hue. They must be distinguished by small multiples, direct labelling and position. That is the cognitively correct answer and it costs the project the lush twelve-colour medium chart that readers associate with richness. Some will read the restraint as thinness.

6. IT BREAKS P1'S MOST RECOGNISABLE SIGNATURE. Anyone arriving from P1 will notice that P2's field is still. Demoting ambient jitter to triggered TREMOR is right on the evidence at n=1,573, but it costs repo-level recognisability, and a reviewer could reasonably call it a break in the house style rather than a scaling rule. I have argued it is a scaling rule; I concede it can be read the other way.

7. THE TRANSPOSE HAS DISCOVERY COST. Clicking a field name to transpose the era card is a novel interaction, and novel interactions are mostly not discovered. The scripted fallback exists, but the fallback is a genuinely worse experience than the transpose, and realistically most readers will only ever get the fallback. If P7 has to be re-scoped, this is the piece I would cut first.

proposals.divergence_from_p1:
Seven items the combined post-P2 review must reconcile.

1. JITTER'S SCOPE RULE. P1 ships ambient measurement jitter on ~160 marks. P2 ships triggered TREMOR, because at 1,573 marks ambient motion stops being texture and becomes an undifferentiated attention-capture field. P1 need not change, but the system doc cannot present jitter as unconditional. Proposed repo rule: uncertainty is carried by geometry by default; motion is a triggered reveal; ambient jitter is permitted only below roughly 300 simultaneous marks.

2. THE AMBER/CYAN SEMANTIC AXIS IS RE-DECLARED. P1: amber = PRICE (market-set, human-chosen), cyan = COST (physical floor). P2: amber = the seller's own number, cyan = an independent number. These are compatible — P1's price was the chosen number and its cost the physical, disinterested one — but they are not identical. My proposed general form for the repo, which covers both projects and is a thesis worth owning: AMBER = THE INTERESTED PARTY'S NUMBER; CYAN = THE DISINTERESTED MEASUREMENT. The review must adopt or reject that generalisation explicitly, because P3 will inherit whichever it picks.

3. TWO NEW TOKENS. Verdigris #4E7A5E (the tripartite third party — neither seller nor buyer) and Paper Wash #E7E1D3 (the fill that means 'not certain'). Both are P2-motivated. I argue both generalise: any project with a three-party structure needs a hue for 'neither,' and every project needs a fill that means uncertainty without becoming a data series. The review decides whether they enter the system or stay project-local.

4. THREE NEW MOTION VERBS against P1's two. TREMOR, RECLASSIFY, STAMP. RECLASSIFY is arguably not new — it is P1's particle morph, named, with a distance-ordered stagger rule added. The review should decide whether it is a verb or a specification of an existing one. STAMP is genuinely new and genuinely needed: P2 makes assertions (grades, era scope) that P1 did not have to punctuate.

5. A NEW FIRST-CLASS STATE: NO READING. P1 never had to draw "the instrument is working correctly and the answer is: not determinable." P2 needs it in three places — era 7's unranked pools, era 1's 38% unassigned residual, and thread 2's era-7 column that cannot be closed. I recommend adopting it repo-wide, because it is the honest complement to error bars and P3 will need it.

6. PROVENANCE GETS A SPATIAL REGISTER, NOT A TOOLTIP. P1 put source grade on the mark, which was right for one effective source. P2 adds a persistent rail board because it has eight incompatible rails and nineteen definitional seams. Proposed general rule: if a project carries more than two sources with different coverage windows, provenance earns its own register; below that, it stays on the mark.

7. WHERE THE METAPHOR HONESTLY STRAINS, RECORDED FOR THE REVIEW. The auction bench is not a measurement — it is a mechanism you run, not a quantity you read. It rejoins the instrument grammar only because its output is a BAND rather than a number, which is the instrument's own language. That is a real stretch and the review should decide whether "the bench" becomes a second repo-level object alongside "the instrument," or whether it stays a P2 idiom. My view: it becomes a second object, because P3 will almost certainly need to let readers run something rather than only read something.
