proposals.divergence_from_p1:
KEPT VERBATIM, and proposed as the repo system's shared base layer: Bone #F2EEE4, Graphite #15181D, Zinc #838A93, Newsreader, Martian Mono, IBM Plex Mono, the SETTLE and SWEEP verbs, particles that snap rather than drift, one-change-at-a-time scene transitions, and light-mode only. P2 is deliberately the same paper with a different apparatus on it.

WHAT THE COMBINED REVIEW MUST RECONCILE:

1. CYAN IS RE-ROLED. #3AA6BD meant COST in P1; it means THE COUNT in P2. The review must decide whether the repo system assigns colour to SEMANTIC ROLES across projects (in which case cyan must mean one thing everywhere and one of us has to move) or to PER-PROJECT ROLE SLOTS (in which case the rule is "cyan is always the second workhorse, whatever that project's second concept is"). I argue for the slot rule, because P1's cost/price pair and P2's money/count pair are structurally the same opposition — a physical quantity against a market quantity — but this must be decided, not drifted into.

2. AMBER MOVES. Filament Amber #E0972A becomes Brass #B07A2C. Same hue family, lower chroma, for particle-density reasons. If the review wants one amber across the repo, it should pick the darker one and P1 should adopt it: P1 has ~160 marks and can afford a darker value, P2 has thousands and cannot afford the lighter one.

3. REDLINE MOVES. #C6432B becomes Rust #A8442E for protanopic separation from brass. Same argument, same direction: pick one, prefer P2's.

4. MEASUREMENT JITTER IS DEMOTED — the biggest divergence. P1 made it the core uncertainty device on every mark. P2 rations it to the 65 claims (13%) whose CI exceeds 60% of the central, and introduces two STATIC registers ahead of it: ribbon WIDTH for interval size and TEXTURE for source grade. The review must rule on whether the repo's uncertainty grammar is motion-primary (P1) or texture-primary-with-motion-rationed (P2). My argument for P2's: motion does not scale past a few hundred marks without becoming wallpaper, and on a time series it mis-encodes epistemic uncertainty as data volatility — a jittering line says the market wobbled. If the review agrees, P1 should adopt width and texture as its resting state and keep jitter for its widest intervals only.

5. THREE NEW MOTION VERBS. CRANK (320ms with a 40ms causal hold), TRAVERSE (arc SETTLE with a fading path trace), and CUT (0ms, for definitional seams). All three are additive rather than conflicting. I propose all three enter the repo vocabulary; CUT in particular is general-purpose — any project with definitional seams needs a verb that means "these two things are not continuous."

6. A FOURTH TYPEFACE. Instrument Sans for architecture and control labels only. This is the most likely thing the review cuts, and the fallback is named: organ labels move to IBM Plex Mono at 500 weight with wider tracking.

7. A NEW STRUCTURAL PRIMITIVE. P1 had no equivalent of the bench floor plan or the organ pull. If the repo hub is built after P2, the organ-pull peek strip is the strongest candidate for a shared navigation pattern across both projects, because both are "one schema, many instances" material.

proposals.name: THE SURVEY
proposals.one_line: One grid that never moves, seven eras laid on it, and ink spent strictly in proportion to evidence.
proposals.philosophy:
A survey is three things at once, and this project is all three. It is an atlas — a fixed graticule reused plate after plate, so two pages can be laid side by side and the coordinates mean the same thing. It is an act of measurement with a declared instrument and a stated error. And it is political: a survey is commissioned by somebody, and the map it produces is what makes the land ownable. That triple meaning is the reason to build P2 comparison-first rather than drama-first.

The cognitive argument is narrow and strong. The four threads are not about quantities rising; they are about POSITIONS IN A STRUCTURE — who counts, who takes a cut, who is admitted, who owns the door. A position is only legible against a frame. If era 3's PRICING cell and era 6's PRICING cell sit at different screen coordinates, comparing them is a working-memory task: encode a value, saccade, scroll, decay, compare. Working memory holds about four chunks and decays in seconds; that comparison fails silently and the reader never knows it failed. If the two cells sit at the same x-position in adjacent rows, the same comparison becomes position-along-a-common-scale — Cleveland & McGill's most accurate elementary perceptual task, and preattentive. Spatial constancy converts comparison from a memory task into a perception task. That single conversion is what the Atlas buys, and it is worth more here than in almost any other project, because this project's entire argument is comparative.

Two governing rules follow, and they do the rest of the work.

INK FOLLOWS EVIDENCE. Solid fill is reserved for grade-A quantities. Grade B gets a stroke and a whisker. Grade C and anything whose 80% CI exceeds 60% of its central gets hatch and no point mark at all. Mark type is a pure function of (grade, ci_ratio), computed in code, not chosen by an author. This is Tufte's data-ink ratio turned into an epistemics rule: visual weight equals evidentiary weight, enforced structurally. The 65 wide-CI claims cannot be drawn as points because the function that draws them has no branch that emits a point.

THE AGENCY MOTION RULE. Motion is the strongest preattentive channel we have; spending it on ambient uncertainty across 1,573 marks makes it worthless. So motion is reserved for one meaning: a number moves on screen if and only if it moves because SOMEONE CHOSE. Bidders shading, a classifier picking a rule, an instrument being swapped. If a number is merely unknown, it does not move — it hatches. Motion equals agency. In a project about institutional power, that is not a decoration; it is the thesis rendered as a physics.
proposals.why_this_project:
Three properties of this specific material make comparison-first the correct choice rather than a stylistic preference.

First, the evidence is structurally uneven in a way that a dramatic direction would have to hide. 133 grade-A claims and 112 grade-C ones, 65 claims whose interval is wider than 60% of their own central, eight compilers measuring four different objects, a fifteen-year hole (2011-2025) sitting exactly where the story peaks, and 77 years at the front with no annual series at all. A drama-first design must either smooth that or apologise for it in captions. An atlas turns it into content: the same cell in seven eras, some solid, some hatched, some empty, is itself the finding. Chapter 9's own conclusion — "the medium mix is the visible change; the money-type mix is the real one" — is a comparison across a fixed frame. The design should be the shape of the argument.

Second, the through-line is a rule that held and then broke. From 1914 to about 1996, someone other than the seller did the counting. Then that stopped. A break in a pattern is only perceptible if the pattern is perceptible, and a pattern is perceptible when seven instances occupy the same slot in the same frame. Gestalt similarity plus one violation is the most reliable "something is wrong here" percept available. The Atlas manufactures the thesis's emotional payload; a narrative essay would have to assert it and hope.

Third, this project keeps having to say "these two numbers are not on the same ruler." Coen billings versus MAGNA media-owner revenue. Era 5's geographic rule versus the unified-intent rule. Dollar share (eras 1-4) versus advertiser head count (eras 5-7). Coen's internet line at 49.7% of IAB's. Billboards becoming Out of Home at 2.77x. A design whose default gesture is "put two things beside each other under a declared frame, and draw the gap between them" answers all of these with one piece of furniture instead of six special cases. The permanent RAIL LANE is that piece of furniture, and it exists because this dataset demanded it.

Where the drama lives — the burden the philosophy brief set. Three named moments, each created BY the comparison rather than despite it. (1) The plumb on MEASUREMENT: seven cells arrive in one column, six name someone who is not the seller, the seventh names the seller. (2) The hundred cents' last bin: 100 particles the reader has tracked across seven eras, and fifteen of them stop being locatable. (3) The empty comb: the data-density strip goes visibly blank across 1840-1918 and again across 2011-2025, the two windows the argument most needs. Drama from absence, drama from a broken row, drama from an object you have followed losing its identity. None of these is available to a design that does not hold the frame still.

hard_problems.solution:
The signature is not a chart, it is a PLATE: a fixed frame, 1440x470 desktop, that four interchangeable engines mount into. The plate's x-axis is 1840-2026, linear, always, in every chapter. Era 1 therefore occupies 42% of the frame permanently. Seven era bands sit behind the plot as #E8E4D8 blocks, labelled in the band's top-left. The reader learns one coordinate system in chapter 1 and reuses it ten times.

Permanent chrome, never removed: a 44px RAIL LANE at the plate's foot showing which compiler's rail each year's number is on, with named end-cap tabs — COEN/McCANN 1919-2007, MAGNA 1980-2025, IAB/PwC 1996-2025, NAA, CENSUS OF MANUFACTURES, and BRIDGE_MCE_MG8 in cross-hatch. Where two rails overlap (1980-2007) they are drawn as two physically separated rails that never touch. Under it, an 8px DENSITY COMB: one 1px tick per year that has at least one datum. Sparse before 1919, visibly thin 2011-2025. Rendering evidence availability as its own series is what makes ds-gap-001 perceptible instead of footnoted.

Four engines, all mounting into the same frame at the same coordinates:
(1) RIBBON PAIR — the default for totals. Each compiler gets a band from CI-low to CI-high with a 1.5px centre stroke and a named end tab. Overlapping years show BOTH. The vertical gap between them at 1980 is annotated with a GAP CALLIPER reading 23.4%, and a second calliper decomposes it: 69% category scope, 7.2 points price basis. There is no splice codepath. Cross-rail interpolation is not implemented — the tween function does not exist, so no future contributor can accidentally produce one.
(2) SMALL-MULTIPLE FIELD — for by-medium. Eleven panels, shared x, shared y, common baseline, sorted by peak year. Not stacked, not a streamgraph.
(3) INDEXED SLOPE — for share-of-GDP. One line per rail, with the 17.4% Coen-to-media-owner restatement drawn as a BRIDGE OFFSET: a hatched vertical step you can toggle on and off, labelled 'part of this fall is the ruler, not the market.'
(4) UNIT FIELD (Canvas) — the object-constancy particle layer, described under P9 thread 2.

The scale readout in the plate's top-right is a Martian Mono numeral that ALWAYS carries its rail name beneath it. There is no state in which a US ad-spend number appears without naming its rail.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Stacked area and streamgraph fail here for a specific perceptual reason, not a stylistic one: middle bands must be judged by thickness measured at a shifting baseline. Cleveland & McGill rank position-along-a-common-scale first and length-at-an-unaligned-baseline far below; area/angle judgments carry roughly two to three times the error. With 27 medium labels and a documented middle-band trap, the encoding would put the largest errors precisely on the media whose slow decline is the story. Small multiples restore a common baseline to every medium at the cost of a smaller plot each — the right trade, because the reader's task here is 'when did this one turn over,' a shape question, not a value question. Sorting by peak year produces a diagonal wave across the field, which makes chapter 1's claim that new media enter small and take decades a shape you SEE rather than a sentence you accept.

The rail lane is justified by Mayer's spatial-contiguity principle: the provenance caveat must be adjacent to the mark it governs, not in a footnote, or the reader integrates the chart without it. Making it permanent furniture rather than a per-chart annotation means the vocabulary is learned once (recognition) instead of re-parsed per chapter (recall). And the density comb exploits a real weakness: humans are poor at perceiving absence — change blindness applies to what is not there. Converting absence into a positive visual quantity (white gaps in a field of ticks) turns a non-perception into a perception.

hard_problems.solution:
Era 1 is not a gap in the spine; it is a different plate type at the same coordinates. Because the x-axis is fixed at 1840-2026 in every chapter, the pre-instrument era holds 42% of the frame permanently and can never be forgotten.

Inside that span the plot shows SOUNDINGS ONLY: the benchmark years (1867 at ~$50M, 1880, 1914 at $1,100-1,302M) as hatched lozenges drawn at their full 80% extent. Between them there is nothing — no dotted line, no interpolation, no faded connector. Empty ruled paper, with one label set in 11px uppercase Plex Sans across the span: 'NO ONE COUNTED THIS YEARLY.' The emptiness is content, and the density comb under it is visibly blank.

The era-1 CHAPTER then rotates the plate into GAZETTEER mode. Instead of a time series, the plate mounts a card field: the roughly twenty benchmark and structural estimates arranged not by year but by what they measure — receipts, print share, agent cut, classified share, addressed catalogues. Each card is a lozenge at its 80% range, its source named, its method one sentence. The reader experiences era 1 as a room of testimony rather than as a chart, which is what the evidence actually is. The spine plate stays visible beneath it with its empty comb.

The continuity device is composition, not level. The hundred-cents particle field (P9 thread 2) runs in era 1 exactly as in every other era: 15 cents to the agent, 85 to the publisher, and a hatched residual for the national special representatives' unknown rate. Era 1's stack cannot be closed either — which is the point, and it sets up era 7's uncloseable stack as a RETURN rather than a novelty. Composition survives where levels do not, so era 1 sits on the spine on the one axis where it has evidence.

One more device: the era-1 band carries the residual honestly. The 1914 four-way money-type row sums to 62%, and the unassigned 38% is drawn as its own hatched block with its own label, not left as a silent gap.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
The naive fix — interpolate a faint dotted line across 1840-1918 — is a Gestalt trap. Good continuation makes the visual system complete a broken contour automatically and preattentively; a dotted line will be perceived as data by most readers regardless of the legend, because closure operates below the level at which legends are consulted. The only reliable defence is to withhold the contour entirely. Empty space adjacent to dense space is itself a strong figure-ground signal.

Holding the axis at 1840 in every chapter uses the frame as external memory (Norman's knowledge-in-the-world). The reader never has to remember that the story starts before the data does; the screen remembers for them, permanently, at a cost of 42% of the frame — a cost this design pays willingly because 'the pre-instrument era is nearly half the story' is a claim the layout can make wordlessly.

And routing era 1's continuity through composition rather than level respects the encoding hierarchy: the era has no defensible position-on-a-common-scale values, but it does have defensible part-of-whole shares, and shares can be shown as fixed-position bins where identity is carried by location rather than by magnitude.

hard_problems.solution:
Replace P1's measurement jitter with a static three-mark GRAMMAR, and keep motion for a different job. Mark type is a pure function of (grade, ci_width/central), computed in the render layer:

BENCHMARK — grade A and ci_ratio <= 0.25. A 7px filled square in --ink with a hairline cross. Sharp edges. Reads as 'you can stand on this.'
STATION — grade B, or grade A with a wider interval, and ci_ratio <= 0.60. A 6px hollow ring on a 1px stem with capped whiskers at the 80% bounds. Crisp edge, interval drawn.
SOUNDING — grade C, OR any claim with ci_ratio > 0.60, whichever fires first. A hatched lozenge whose long axis IS the 80% interval. 45-degree hatch at 2px pitch in --hatch #9AA0A6. NO point mark. The central appears only as a 1px internal tick, and the tick's tooltip label is the word 'centre', never 'value'.
CONSTRUCTED — any of our own bridged or derived values (the 28 bridged points, the money-type splits). Same lozenge, CROSS-hatched at 45 and 135 degrees. This separates 'grade C from a source' from 'grade C because we built it', which the reader must be able to tell apart.

The 65 wide-CI claims are unrepresentable as points because no branch of the function emits a point for them. A permanent 90px GRADE KEY sits in the plate's lower-left in every chapter, three marks, three plain sentences: 'A — a filing or an official record. B — credible reporting. C — our own estimate.'

Every mark's tooltip carries central, 80% CI, grade, compiler, as-of date, and one gate-passing sentence, e.g. 'Best guess $230.9bn. Could be $211bn to $244bn. Our own bridge, not a published number.'

Motion is reserved by the AGENCY MOTION RULE: a value moves on screen only when a person or an institution CHOSE it. Bidders shading in the simulator move. The taxonomy switch moves. The instrument switch moves. Epistemic uncertainty never moves; it hatches.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Three reasons to diverge from jitter, all about scale rather than taste. First, numerosity: P1 had a handful of hero numerals; P2 has 1,573 series points plus 505 claims. Motion is the top-priority preattentive channel (Ware) — if 1,573 marks all vibrate, motion stops signalling anything and becomes texture, and the design has spent its most powerful channel on ambient state. Second, expressiveness: jitter can encode interval width and nothing else. P2's uncertainty is often not statistical at all — it is basis uncertainty (which rail), classification uncertainty (which rule), and non-existent orderings. No amplitude can say 'this pair has no order.' A shape vocabulary can, because shapes can be joined, bracketed and left open. Third, integrity under capture: a jittering chart screenshotted is a chart with a false point estimate in it. Given this project's audience will screenshot, the honest state must be the resting state.

The grammar's design follows Bertin's separability: shape and texture are separable from position and from hue, so uncertainty is readable without competing with the categorical and quantitative channels. And hatch specifically is the right texture for 'less evidence' because perceived visual weight scales with ink coverage — a hatched lozenge is literally lighter than a filled square, so the INK FOLLOWS EVIDENCE rule is not a convention the reader must learn but a percept they already have.

What is lost: jitter's aliveness, which genuinely helped P1. Recovered elsewhere — the particle fields and the simulator carry all the liveness this piece needs, and they carry it where motion means something.

hard_problems.solution:
The era-5 taxonomy pair is treated as a RECLASSIFICATION EVENT, not a data seam, and it is built on the hundred-cents particle layer so that object constancy does the teaching.

The plate shows the year 2000 as four bins at four fixed x-positions, in the order used everywhere else in the essay: NATIONAL BRAND / LOCAL RETAIL / CLASSIFIED / DIRECT RESPONSE. Above them, a two-position switch labelled in plain words rather than in jargon:
  'Count phone-book money by WHO BOUGHT IT'  (era-native, geographic)
  'Count phone-book money by WHY IT WAS BOUGHT'  (cross-era comparable, unified intent)

Flip it and exactly 4.5 particles' worth — the local Yellow Pages block, $11,135M, 4.4995 points of the 2000 market — travel from LOCAL RETAIL to DIRECT RESPONSE under the RECLASSIFY verb. Nothing else moves. Not one other particle. The travelling cents carry a 12%-opacity ghost trail back to their origin bin, and a counter reads '4.5 cents in 100 moved. Nothing else changed.'

Above the bins sits the layer that stops the flip being misread as news. Both pools are drawn as SOUNDINGS on a shared horizontal share axis with their 80% intervals: 28.32 vs 24.71 under one rule, 23.82 vs 29.21 under the other. In BOTH states the lozenges overlap, so in both states an UNRANKED BRACE joins them, carrying: 'These two cannot be put in order. The rule below decides which centre is bigger. The evidence does not.'

The order indicator — which pool is 'ahead' — is rendered inside a boxed field explicitly labelled 'SET BY THE RULE, NOT BY THE MARKET.' Naming the artifact as an artifact, and giving it its own enclosure, is stronger than suppressing it.

The switch is sticky and global. Its state persists across the essay, and any chart elsewhere that touches era 5 shows the current rule in its header. Cross-era comparisons force the unified-intent rule and say so, per the freeze note: splicing era 5's geographic shares to era 6 or 7 crosses an undocumented redefinition worth 4.50 points, so the app refuses it.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
This problem is a category-membership change wearing the costume of a value change, and the reader's default error is to read it as 'the market changed.' Two Gestalt mechanisms are recruited to block that error. Common fate: particles that move together are perceived as ONE object, which is exactly the correct percept — a single identifiable block of directory money, not a diffuse revision. And motion-as-sole-change exploits attention capture in the right direction: because everything else is frozen, the only moving thing is the only lesson, so gaze goes there without instruction. This is Mayer's signalling principle implemented as physics rather than as an arrow.

Object constancy is the load-bearing choice. If the two taxonomies were shown as two charts, or as a cross-fade, the reader would compare two IMAGES and have to infer the transformation. With persistent particles they WATCH the transformation, which converts an inference into a perception — the standing preference for object-constant unit visualisation earns its keep precisely here, at the project's hardest definitional moment.

Placing the overlap test ABOVE the switch, so it is read first, matters for order effects: anchoring means whichever ordering is seen first becomes the default belief. Establishing 'unranked' before showing the flip means the flip arrives as a demonstration of arbitrariness rather than as a finding to be anchored on.

hard_problems.solution:
THE OVERLAP FIELD, with a shuffle and exactly one order assertion.

Era 7's four pools are drawn on a single horizontal axis — share of US ad spend, 0-50% — each as a hatched SOUNDING lozenge spanning its full 80% interval: national brand 25-47%, local and retail 15-31%, classified 1.4-6.8%, direct response 29.5-47%. They are stacked vertically only for legibility, never for meaning.

Three devices make the unrankedness true rather than merely stated:

(1) THE SHUFFLE. On scroll-in, the three unranked pools visibly permute — a 900ms staggered swap, 60ms per row, then a hard stop — with the caption 'These three are in no order. This page put them in one at random.' The vertical order is genuinely randomised per session. The reader can reload and watch it change. Unrankedness becomes a property they can TEST, not a claim they must accept.

(2) THE ORDER RULE. One 1px vertical --ink line at classified's CI-high (6.8%), the single ordering the evidence establishes, carrying two short sentences: 'Everything above this line beats classified. Above the line, nothing can be ordered.' One line, one assertion, checkable.

(3) THE UNRANKED BRACE. Hover or tap any two lozenges above the line and a brace joins them with the overlap in points — 'overlap: 4.5 points. Cannot be ordered.' The brace is the same object used at the era-5 taxonomy pair and at the era-5 national/direct-response pair, so it is a learned vocabulary item by the time era 7 arrives.

What is forbidden, in code: no stacked bar, no sorted list, no ranked legend, no 'top pool' callout for any set containing two unranked members. The sort comparator for money-type pools throws unless the caller passes an explicit ordering certificate from reconciled.json. Chapter 9's own sentence — 'Brand money and response money sit 1.4 points apart and cannot be ranked against each other at all' — is the caption.

The same field type is reused for era 5's national_brand/direct_response pair and for the 1914 row, where only one ordering is safe (classified was smallest). The 1914 row therefore renders with FOUR lozenges, one order rule, and a visible unassigned-38% block.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
The trap is that position-along-a-common-scale is our BEST perceptual channel, which means readers will extract ordinal information from vertical arrangement whether or not you intend them to. You cannot legend your way out of a preattentive inference. The only reliable countermeasures are to remove the channel or to demonstrate its meaninglessness by exercising it — the shuffle does the second, which is stronger, because it converts a disclaimer into evidence the reader generates themselves. Self-generated evidence resists later distortion in memory far better than asserted caveats.

Overlapping intervals are also where readers most reliably over-infer: given two error bars that overlap, most people still report the one with the higher central as 'bigger.' Removing the point marks entirely (soundings, not dots) removes the object the comparison would attach to. There is no dot to be higher than another dot; there are two hatched extents and a brace.

The single ORDER RULE line is a deliberate application of the principle that one explicit, bounded assertion is safer than an emergent one. Layout-implied orderings are unbounded — every pair in the layout implies a relation. A vertical rule implies exactly one relation, states it in words, and leaves everything else visibly unclaimed.

hard_problems.solution:
THE BENCH — a four-cell fixed frame that never changes position across all 21 scenarios. The Atlas discipline applied to an interactive: same slots, same places, every time.

A. THE PAGE (top-left) — allocation. Two ad slots, three named cards (Aster Auto Cover, Brindle Brokers, Cedar Cover) which are the SAME three DOM objects across all 21 scenarios; they reorder, they are never replaced. Above them, 100 impression particles (1 particle = 10 impressions) fall down the page. Particles that click turn amber and drop into the ledger.
B. THE LEDGER (top-right) — money, three permanent Martian Mono numerals in fixed positions: REVENUE / CLICKS / PRICE PER CLICK. Plus a permanent fourth field, WHO CHOSE THIS, naming for the current state which quantity is set by the seller, which by the bidder, which by the rule.
C. THE RULE (bottom-left) — every knob, always visible; knobs a scenario does not use are dimmed but present. ranking_rule, pricing_rule, gamma, format_multiplier, reserve, predicted_ctrs, bid_increment, rgsp_uplift, stickage, bidder_mode.
D. THE BAND (bottom-right) — the permanent honesty panel. A horizontal band from $440 (lowest envy-free) to $760 (naive truthful), band_ratio 1.727, with a marker at the current position. EVERY revenue number elsewhere on the bench carries a small band-position glyph. There is no state in which a revenue figure appears without it.

The central teaching — sc-01 to sc-03 — is delivered as one perceptual event rather than as a table. Switch from pure_bid to quality_weighted and the amber click-particles go from 18 to 58 while the height each falls (price per click) drops from $1.57 to $0.91. Total area, which is revenue, rises from $28.18 to $52.58 per thousand. More particles, each shorter, more total ink. The sign everyone gets backwards is a shape.

sc-04 and sc-05: the shading toggle is a three-position control, not a slider, exactly as the params specify. Watch the $10 bidder drop from slot 1 to slot 2 and its own payoff rise $400 to $640 while seller revenue falls $760 to $660 to $440. THE BAND marker walks left as the bidders get better. Caption: 'Same rule. Same bidders. $440 to $760, depending only on how well they play.'

sc-06 and sc-09 carry LOCKED CAPTIONS — non-dismissible, always on screen when active — reproducing the required_caption strings verbatim. And the guard against teaching a dead mechanism is a CONSTRAINT, not a warning: the bench's title bar carries a SEARCH / DISPLAY pill. With SEARCH lit, pricing_rule = first_price is not selectable; the control is disabled and its tooltip reads 'Search never moved to first price. The 2019 search change was rGSP.' Making the wrong combination unbuildable beats labelling it wrong. sc-10 gets a permanent two-panel SPLIT RULE graphic: one year, two arrows, opposite directions, 0.0% and +5.74%, with the band-traversal figure of 7.9%.

sc-07's separation is spatial and thematic: predicted_ctr lives in C (THE RULE — the seller's cell), true_ctr lives in A (THE PAGE — the world's cell), and a connector draws the gap. The break-even at 1.99% is a marked stop on the slider. That is thread 1 embedded inside the simulator: the seller's own estimate sits at the centre of the mechanism.

Navigation for 21 scenarios: two plates, not one list. THE YIELD ENGINE (sc-01 to sc-10) and THE VOLUME ENGINE (D1 to D11), each indexed as four lesson-groups of two or three, so the reader never faces more than five choices at a level.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Twenty-one scenarios is roughly five times working-memory span, so a flat stepper guarantees the reader loses the thread; Hick's law also makes a 21-item chooser slow enough to be abandoned. Two plates of four groups keeps every decision at or under five options and gives the two engines the structural separation chapter 7 insists on — the auction is the yield engine, distribution is the volume engine, and 'the first paid for the second.'

The fixed four-cell frame is the same argument as the era matrix: a control layout learned once becomes recognition rather than recall, and dimmed-but-present knobs teach the full instrument in scenario one. Hiding irrelevant controls would reduce clutter but destroy the reader's model of what the mechanism CAN do — which matters enormously here, because the chapter's final claim is that the mechanism did not need replacing, only tuning. You cannot feel that unless you can see the tuning knobs the whole time.

The particle rendering of the sign flip is the highest-value encoding decision in the simulator. Three numbers in a table (revenue +86.6%, clicks +222%, price/click -42%) require the reader to hold three ratios and notice their signs disagree — three chunks plus a relation, right at the span limit, and the counterintuitive part is exactly the part that gets dropped. Rendered as count-versus-height-versus-area, the disagreement is a single glance: the pile got wider and flatter and bigger. Object constancy across the switch (impressions are conserved; only their fate changes) is what makes the two states comparable rather than merely sequential.

THE BAND as permanent chrome is an anti-anchoring device. Any single revenue figure invites the reader to treat it as THE revenue of the mechanism, which is the precise error the equilibrium band refutes. Attaching a band-position glyph to every figure means the reader can never encode a number without also encoding its contingency.

hard_problems.solution:
First, an editorial resolution the design needs and the schema implies: EVENTS is not a comparable field. It is the era's own spine, and it lives on the plate's time axis as tick marks, not in a cell. That leaves eight genuinely comparable fields — CREATORS, BUYERS, SELLERS, MEDIUM, SCALE, PRICING, MEASUREMENT, TARGETING — and 8 x 7 = 56 cells exactly.

Three artefacts, one structure.

(1) THE PLATE HEADER — the repeating per-era scaffold. Every era chapter opens with the same 8-cell strip: 4 columns x 2 rows, 110px tall, identical geometry in all seven chapters. Each cell carries the field name in 10px uppercase Plex Sans, one number in IBM Plex Mono, one phrase of six words or fewer, and a grade dot. Same order, same size, same position, seven times.

(2) THE MATRIX — the essay's gazetteer and its table of contents, reachable from every screen. The full 8x7 grid on one screen, cells 60x44px, each carrying one numeral and a grade dot, columns labelled with the era names and rows with the field names. This is the overview-first surface: the reader always knows where they are in the structure, which is the standard cure for getting lost in a long scrollytelling piece.

(3) PLUMB — the answer to 'how does a reader compare era 3's PRICING to era 6's without scrolling twice.' They do not scroll. They press a field name, or the number key 1-8. The seven eras' cells for that field slide into a single seven-row column, all other cells collapsing to 4px rules, 380ms on cubic-bezier(.32,0,.15,1) — fast start, hard stop, a plumb bob dropping and being caught. Now 180 years of PRICING is one screen, in order, era-labelled. Press again to return. Era selection stays locked while plumbed, so the reader can traverse eras with the column held.

The MEASUREMENT column is the essay's climax and is described under P9.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Eight fields exceeds the four-chunk working-memory span, which is why an eight-item list would fail — but it sits inside the seven-plus-or-minus-two range for a list that can be LEARNED, and the design never asks the reader to hold it as a list. Fixing the eight cells in identical screen positions across seven chapters converts them from remembered items into a learned layout: after two eras the reader knows where PRICING is the way they know where a car's indicator stalk is. That is the difference between recall and recognition, and it is worth roughly an order of magnitude in retrieval reliability.

PLUMB is the design's core cognitive claim made operable. Comparing era 3's PRICING to era 6's across a scrolled document requires encoding, holding across an interruption, and retrieving — and the interruption (scrolling past three chapters) is long enough to destroy the encoded value without the reader noticing the loss. Bringing the two cells into simultaneous view converts that failure-prone memory operation into a single perceptual judgment. Simultaneity beats sequence for comparison, always; the only question is whether you can afford the screen, and a 60x44 cell means you can afford seven of them.

Demoting EVENTS out of the matrix is not a dodge. Events are not comparable across eras — they are dated singulars, and dated singulars belong on a time axis where their spacing is meaningful. Forcing them into a cell would have made spacing meaningless and invited false parallelism between, say, the 1962 upfront and the 2019 rGSP launch.

hard_problems.solution:
The Atlas degrades better than the alternatives, because a fixed grid collapses to a fixed column without losing its rule. The mobile path, at 375px:

The spine plate becomes a TOP-LOCKED BAND, 38vh, prose scrolling under it. Same x-axis, same era bands, same rail lane at 32px, same density comb at 6px. Nothing about the coordinate system changes, so a reader who has seen desktop recognises mobile and vice versa.

The 8-cell plate header becomes 2 columns x 4 rows, row-major, preserving reading order.

PLUMB becomes SWIPE, and is better on touch than on desktop. Swipe left/right on the plate moves between eras with the field column held. The field row stays fixed at the top; only the era changes. The core comparative act survives, reshaped from simultaneous to sequential-with-a-frozen-frame.

The small-multiple field renders as 11 panels in 3 columns at 44px tall, shared y. Legible because the task is shape, not value. Tap promotes one panel to full width.

THE BENCH collapses to a vertical two-cell: THE PAGE over THE LEDGER, with THE BAND as a permanent 28px strip between them and THE RULE as a bottom sheet. Free-parameter exploration is DROPPED. Instead, the 21 scenarios become a swipeable deck of prebuilt states with exactly ONE live knob each — the knob that scenario is about. sc-09's three-knob stacking is unavailable on mobile and says so.

The hundred-cents field survives intact (100 particles is cheap); ghost trails are dropped and frame rate is capped at 30fps under Battery Saver.

Deliberately dropped, and named in a 'what this device does not do' note reachable from the menu: hover tooltips (replaced by tap-to-pin, one pinned mark at a time); the full 8x7 matrix simultaneously (replaced by a 2-column scroll with sticky field labels); the rail lane's end-cap tabs (replaced by a tappable legend); multi-knob simulator exploration; custom bid entry; the gamma x format stacking panel.

Two hard mobile rules. No annotation is ever overlaid on a chart below 640px — every callout moves to a caption block directly beneath the plate. And every visual carries a mandatory alt_sentence in the data layer, written to pass the four readability gates, driving a TEXT-ONLY toggle that swaps every plate for its plain-sentence equivalent. That toggle is the accessibility path, the low-bandwidth path, and the honest fallback all at once.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Overlaid text on a 375px chart is the single most common mobile data-journalism failure, and it is a figure-ground failure: at that size, label and mark compete for the same pixels, and the visual system resolves the competition by degrading both. Moving all annotation below the plate costs vertical space and buys legibility outright.

Swipe-with-frozen-frame is the right mobile analogue because it preserves the one thing that matters — the coordinate system — while accepting the one degradation that is unavoidable: comparison becomes sequential, and sequential comparison is a memory operation. That is a genuine loss and I name it in the sacrifices rather than pretending parity. What mitigates it is that the frame is IDENTICAL between swipes, so only the delta needs encoding, which is roughly the cheapest possible version of a memory comparison.

Dropping simulator free parameters is a deliberate application of constraint-over-instruction. On a touch surface with no hover state and no precise pointer, a nine-knob panel produces states the reader cannot interpret and cannot undo. One knob per scenario keeps every state legible and every lesson intact — the scenarios were designed to teach specific propositions, and each proposition needs one variable, not nine.

hard_problems.solution:
THREAD 1 — WHO COUNTED, AND WHO PAID THE COUNTER. I argue against the two-track timeline and propose THE INDEPENDENCE TRACK: one track, with an ordinal y-axis of three rows — OUTSIDER COUNTS / BOTH SIDES PAY / THE SELLER COUNTS. Each counting institution is a horizontal bar spanning its active years, placed on the row matching who funded it: ABC 1914 (outsider, tripartite), CAB 1930 advertiser-funded, Hooper 1934 rival-medium-funded, Nielsen from 1950 (both sides), the Broadcast Rating Council 1964 (industry), DART's log from the mid-1990s (seller), Google's own click validation and Analytics from 2005 (seller), Facebook's video metric and the MRC's 19-month suspension (seller / nobody). Funder identity beyond the three rows is carried by a text label on each bar's left cap, not by colour.

The result is one shape: bars sit in the top row from 1914 to about 1996 and then FALL to the bottom row and stay there. Eighty-two years of plateau and one drop, as a single perceptual gestalt.

The two natural experiments get SHOCK CALLIPERS in --alarm #B3322B, the only red in the essay besides era 7's unknown bin. At 1987 a calliper drops into an inset: measured prime-time audience -10% overnight, CBS -13%, ABC -13%. At 2021: >=$468M of lost national ad revenue. And 1987 carries the essay's signature control, THE INSTRUMENT SWITCH — two positions, 'diary and meter' / 'people meter', caption 'Same viewing. Two instruments. Two prices.' Nothing about the audience changes on screen; only the readout does.

THREAD 2 — THE INTERMEDIARY'S CUT. THE HUNDRED CENTS, and the project's object-constancy spine. 100 Canvas particles, one per cent of the advertiser's gross outlay under a declared convention printed permanently in the header. Seven bins at seven FIXED screen positions in every era: AGENT/AGENCY, PUBLISHER/NETWORK, STATION/AFFILIATE, REP FIRM, PLATFORM, FRONT-DOOR OWNER, NOT ACCOUNTED FOR. Era by era the same 100 cents re-sort. Era 1: 15 to the agent, 85 to the publisher, and a hatched residual because the national special representatives' rate is unknown. Era 2: 15 agency, 62 network, 23 stations. Era 4: the Economic Census correction — commissions actually received were 14.13/13.92/14.16/13.18% then 10.98% in 1997, so the 'the commission died in the 1980s' story is visibly wrong in the particle field. Era 7: the last bin is hatched, has no floor, and 15 cents drift into it and LOSE THEIR EDGES. The reader has tracked those cents for seven eras. The ending lands because era 1 also had hatch — the piece closes on a return, with more measurement and less knowledge.

THREAD 3 — WHO WAS ALLOWED TO BUY. THE GATE CARD MATRIX as primary. Seven columns, one per era; four rows: DEPOSIT / MINIMUM SPEND / REVIEW / TIME TO LIVE. Cells are numbers or the word 'unknown' in hatch. Era 6's column is the only SPLIT column in the matrix — Overture (10c minimum bid, $20/month, human review) beside AdWords ($5 one-off, no minimum, automated) — and the fork is the finding. Below it, the two panels the evidence forbids joining: left, the classified and directory dollar share sitting at 3-13% from era 1 to era 4; right, the advertiser head count 3,800 to 53,000 to 80,000 to ~1M (drawn as a SOUNDING, 550k-2.6M) to >10M, on a log axis labelled as log. Between them, a designed 24px hatched GUTTER: 'Different rulers. Do not read across.' The gutter is an object, not an absence.

THREAD 4 — THE RENT ON THE FRONT DOOR. THE TOLL PLATES. Seven identical small multiples, each one bar: what the seller paid the front-door owner as a share of the revenue it generated, all on one shared 0-100% scale — 27% affiliate compensation, 5-20% station reps (drawn as a sounding, no central), 56% Overture TAC, 85% AOL, 36% Apple's Safari rate. Absolute dollars do NOT get a second axis; dual axes are a documented mislead. They appear as a Martian Mono numeral at a fixed corner position in each plate, plus one continuous AREA STRIP beneath all seven, log-scaled and labelled as log, where $26.3B in 2021 swamps everything. Inset: the AOL warrant, two lozenges on a log axis — carried at $13.871M, realised ~$1,134.6M — joined by a calliper reading 11.3x, with the famous $100M cash guarantee drawn as a HATCHED lozenge because it is grade B and unfalsifiable. The reversal is the point: the famous number is the soft one.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Thread 1's redesign is the substantive argument. A two-track timeline encodes 'who paid' as categorical colour over time, and seven categorical colours is past the reliable separability limit at small sizes — roughly four to six hues survive small marks, adjacency effects and colour-vision deficiency. Worse, colour is a nominal channel: it can say who, but not how far. The finding is not 'the funder changed identity'; it is 'the counter stopped being independent of the seller.' That is an ORDINAL quantity — distance from the seller — and ordinal quantities belong on position, the most accurate channel available. Moving independence to the y-axis converts a colour-recall task into a shape-perception task, and produces the plateau-and-drop as a single figure. Colour then does the small job it is good at: three states, high-contrast, colourblind-safe.

Thread 2's hundred cents is where the standing preference for object-constant unit visualisation pays its largest dividend. Seven separate stacked bars would show seven compositions and require the reader to infer six transitions. Persistent particles show one population being repeatedly re-sorted, so transformation is perceived rather than inferred. And the final bin works on a mechanism no static chart has: identity loss. A particle you have tracked for seven scenes losing its edge is an event, not a value.

Thread 3's gutter is spatial-separation-as-argument. Proximity is the strongest Gestalt grouping cue, so two panels placed adjacently WILL be read as one series regardless of axis labels. The only reliable defence is to insert a competing figure between them — a hatched band that is itself an object, breaking proximity and continuation at once.

Thread 4 refuses the dual axis for the standard reason — two y-scales let the designer choose the crossing point and therefore choose the story — and recovers the punch by giving magnitude its own dedicated, explicitly-labelled log strip. Separating the two questions ('what share' and 'how much') into two aligned displays keeps each comparison on a common scale, which is exactly what a dual axis destroys.

palette.role: page ground; survey paper. A half-step cooler and lighter than P1's bone so the projects read as siblings, not twins.
plate interior. One value lighter than ground so every chart frame floats without needing a shadow or a heavy border.
primary ink: prose, axes, BENCHMARK marks, the ORDER RULE line. Inherited from P1 verbatim — ink should be shared repo-wide.
secondary text: axis labels, captions, field names, the deck. 6.2:1 on plate.
graticule at 22px pitch, cell borders, hairlines, the matrix grid. Structure that must be present but never read.
amber, workhorse one: THE SELLER'S OWN NUMBER — self-reported, self-audited, seller-funded. Hue inherited from P1, meaning reassigned.
teal, workhorse two: SOMEONE ELSE'S NUMBER — independently counted or outsider-funded. P1's #3AA6BD darkened to clear 4.3:1 at 1.5px hairline widths on plate.
not a hex: a 45-degree half-amber/half-teal fill for jointly funded counting (ABC 1914, the Broadcast Rating Council). Texture rather than a third hue, so the categorical-colour budget stays at two.

the stroke of ALL hatching — soundings, residuals, unknown blocks, the thread-3 gutter. Deliberately low-contrast (~2.9:1 on plate): legible as texture, never as emphasis. This is what INK FOLLOWS EVIDENCE looks like.
the seven era bands behind every plot, alternating with --plate. The one piece of chrome present in literally every chart in the essay.
reserved red. Spent exactly three times in the whole essay: the 1987 shock, the 2021 shock, and era 7's 'not accounted for' bin. Scarcity is what makes it preattentive.

proposals.type:
Four families, two superfamilies.

NEWSREADER (variable, 400/500, optical size on) — body prose only. Inherited from P1 and correctly so: the readability gate demands prose that is pleasant to read at length, and Newsreader's generous x-height and low stroke contrast hold up at 21px/1.6 in a 620px measure. Deck at 21px/1.5 in --ink-2; body at 19px/1.68. Hero question at 58px/1.06.

MARTIAN MONO (500/600) — hero numerals ONLY, at 28px and above. Inherited from P1, where numbers are the protagonists. Used for the ledger's three figures, the plate's scale readout, the toll plates' corner dollars, the calliper values. Its wide sidebearings are an asset at 28px+ and a liability below, which is why it stops there.

IBM PLEX MONO (400/500, tabular figures) — every numeral below 16px: matrix cells, axis ticks, tooltips, the plate header's per-field numbers, the rail lane's year ranges. Chosen over Martian Mono for density: a 60x44px matrix tile has to hold a five-character number and a grade dot, and Plex Mono's narrower advance width makes that fit at 12px without tracking games. True tabular figures mean columns of numbers align down the matrix without manual kerning.

IBM PLEX SANS (400/500/600) — all labels, field names, small caps, captions, chart annotation, UI. Field names render as 10px uppercase at 0.12em tracking; chapter chrome at 11px uppercase at 0.14em. Sans is non-negotiable for on-chart annotation: serifs at 10px over a 22px graticule lose their terminals and the text stops reading as text.

The Plex pair share a skeleton and metrics, so a mono numeral sitting inside a sans label aligns on the baseline and the x-height without adjustment — which matters because the matrix does exactly that 56 times on one screen. Four families is one more than ideal; the justification is that two of them are one superfamily and two are inherited repo assets.
proposals.motion:
Five named verbs, and two deliberate stillnesses.

TRAVERSE — 520ms, cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1). Horizontal, register-preserving movement between eras. The x-axis does NOT rescale and the plate does not redraw; only the era highlight band and the mounted marks move. Named for a surveyor's traverse: you walk the line, you do not move the line.

PLUMB — 380ms, cubic-bezier(.32,0,.15,1). Fast start, hard stop. The seven era cells for one field drop into a single column while everything else collapses to 4px rules. A plumb bob released and caught. This is the signature verb.

SETTLE — 600-900ms, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1). Inherited from P1 verbatim, deliberately: one shared primitive keeps the repo coherent. Any value arriving at its measured position.

RECLASSIFY — ~1,100ms, cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1), duration scaled to travel distance rather than fixed. Slow-in, slow-out, because the reader must be able to TRACK individual particles; multiple-object tracking degrades sharply past roughly 8 degrees of visual angle per second, so the timing is set by the geometry, not by taste. Used only for the era-5 taxonomy switch and the hundred-cents era transitions. Only the moving particles move.

SHUFFLE — 900ms total, staggered 60ms per row, cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), 200ms hold, hard stop. Deliberately slightly loose so it reads as shaking a box rather than as sorting one. Used only on unranked pools.

The two stillnesses are as load-bearing as the verbs. Marks NEVER idle-animate — there is no jitter, no drift, no breathing. And rails never morph into each other: a rail may fade in or out, it may never tween into another rail, and the cross-rail interpolation function is not implemented, so the splice cannot be written by accident later.

PREFERS-REDUCED-MOTION:
TRAVERSE becomes an instant cut with a 120ms opacity cross-fade on the highlight band only.
PLUMB becomes instant replacement, no slide.
SETTLE becomes instant placement.
SHUFFLE is replaced by a genuinely randomised order chosen at load plus the static caption 'These three are in no order. This page put them in one at random.' The ORDER RULE line does the real work either way, so nothing is lost.
RECLASSIFY is the one verb that cannot become a cut, because the entire lesson is WHICH particles moved. Its fallback is a static ghost-and-arrow: the origin bin shows 4.5 hatched ghost cents with a short arrow to the destination bin, plus the counter '4.5 cents in 100 moved. Nothing else changed.' Same lesson, same count, no motion.
Particle fields render a single static frame. Since nothing ever idle-animated, there is nothing to switch off — which is the quiet advantage of having replaced jitter with a static grammar in the first place.
proposals.signature_interaction:
PLUMB, and what you find at the bottom of it.

Press a field name — or the number key 1-8 — anywhere in the essay. The seven eras' cells for that field drop into one column, seven rows, 180 years on one screen, everything else collapsing to 4px rules. 380ms, hard stop. Press again and it releases. This is the comparative act made physical, and the reader will do it dozens of times.

Then plumb on MEASUREMENT, and the Atlas hands you its climax.

Seven rows arrive. Six of them name a counter who is not the seller: the Audit Bureau of Circulations, funded by publishers, advertisers and agencies together, 1914. The Cooperative Analysis of Broadcasting, funded by ADVERTISERS at $70 a month, $33,045 in its first year. Hooper, funded by MAGAZINE PUBLISHERS who thought radio was overstating itself, running about 20% below CAB. Nielsen, sold to both sides. The Broadcast Rating Council, industry-funded, 1964, born out of the Harris hearings. The seventh row names the seller.

Six rows share a shape; the seventh breaks it. That is a Gestalt similarity violation, and it is the most reliable 'something is wrong here' percept the visual system has. It arrives before any sentence has been read.

And row four — 1987 — is drawn in the reserved red, and it carries a switch.

THE INSTRUMENT SWITCH. Two positions: 'diary and meter' / 'people meter'. Flip it. The audience does not change. Nothing about anyone's viewing changes. The measured prime-time network audience falls about 10% and the price falls with it: CBS -13%, ABC -13%, make-goods owed in scatter worth more than the upfront that sold them. Caption, three sentences, all short: 'Same viewing. Two instruments. Two prices.'

That is the whole project in one control, and the Atlas is what delivered the reader to it. The comparison did not compete with the drama. The comparison WAS the route to it.
proposals.what_it_sacrifices:
Eight honest costs, in rough order of how much they hurt.

1. There is no shareable image of 180 years. By refusing to splice Coen to MAGNA, this direction gives up the single line from 1919 to 2026 that would have been the piece's most circulated artefact. A ribbon pair with a 23.4% gap and a calliper is correct and unshareable. That is a real cost in reach, paid deliberately, and a dramatic direction would not pay it.

2. The first screen is cold. No hero animation, no particle bloom, no big moving area chart. A very wide, mostly empty timeline and a grid. Some readers will bounce in three seconds, and the design has no answer for them beyond the question in the headline.

3. Comparison-first rewards operating the piece. A reader who only scrolls gets a decent essay and misses the best of it, because PLUMB is a press and the shuffle is a scroll-in they may skim past. Auto-plumbing at the three dramatic moments mitigates this; it does not remove it.

4. Uncertainty is less charming than P1's jitter. Hatch is honest, static and dull. P1's shimmer was a delight and made the rigour layer feel alive; this direction trades that charm for scale-honesty and screenshot-honesty across 2,000+ marks.

5. Austerity. Two hues, a split fill, hatch and one reserved red will look researchy next to a Reuters or NYT piece with a full categorical ramp. The discipline is defensible; the impression is drier.

6. The frame has to be taught. Chapter 1 must spend real space introducing eight fields, three mark types and a rail lane before the matrix pays off — space not spent on story. The payoff compounds over ten chapters, but the first chapter carries the whole loan.

7. Mobile is genuinely a lesser version, not an equal one. Swipe-with-frozen-frame turns simultaneous comparison into sequential comparison, which moves the work from perception back into memory — the exact conversion this whole direction exists to avoid. The frame being identical between swipes makes it the cheapest possible memory comparison, but it is still a memory comparison.

8. The simulator resists play. Fixed cells, always-visible-but-dimmed knobs, locked captions and a SEARCH/DISPLAY lockout mean a reader who wants to break the model mostly cannot. That is correct — the thing they would break it into is a mechanism that never existed — but it costs the piece some of the delight that a true sandbox would have.

And one thing this direction is honestly worse at than a narrative direction would be: it cannot do a slow reveal. Everything is on the grid from the start, so there is no held-back surprise, no 'and then the chart transforms.' Its drama is structural — a broken row, a lost particle, an empty comb — which is quieter than a reveal and will not work on every reader.
