proposals.divergence_from_p1:
Six items the later combined review must reconcile. Five are cheap; the first two are real.

1. THE WORKHORSE PAIR'S SEMANTICS — the significant one. P1 assigns amber #E0972A to PRICE (market-set, human-chosen) and cyan #3AA6BD to COST (physical floor). P2 keeps the same two hues and reassigns them: amber is THE SELLER'S OWN NUMBER, teal is SOMEONE ELSE'S NUMBER. Both projects claim the pair as 'the one colourblind-safe workhorse pair', and they mean different things by it. Three options: (a) promote the pair to an abstract repo-wide opposition that subsumes both readings — endogenous-to-the-actor versus exogenous-to-the-actor covers price/cost and seller-counted/outsider-counted, and would be my recommendation; (b) accept project-local semantics and require every project to keep a permanent on-screen legend, which P2 already does via the grade key and rail lane; (c) give P2 a different pair, which I would resist because the amber/teal opposition is genuinely load-bearing for thread 1. Recommend (a) plus (b).

2. THE UNCERTAINTY DEVICE. P1's measurement jitter and P2's static three-mark grammar cannot both be 'the house device' — one animates uncertainty, the other freezes it. Proposed unified rule for the review: the house principle is 'uncertainty is always encoded, never hidden', and the ENCODER is a function of mark count. Under roughly 50 simultaneous marks, jitter (it is delightful, and it is legible at that density). Above it, the static grammar (motion salience collapses, and screenshots become dishonest). That rule justifies both projects' choices from one premise rather than declaring one of them a mistake. P2 additionally introduces the AGENCY MOTION RULE — motion means someone chose — which P1 does not contradict but does not state; the review should decide whether it becomes repo-wide.

3. CYAN'S EXACT VALUE. P2 darkens #3AA6BD to #2E7F96 because the original clears only about 2.6:1 at 1.5px hairline widths on a light plate. The review should decide whether the repo token is a hue with lightness steps (recommended: a base and a 'hairline' step) or a fixed hex.

4. THE GROUND. P1 bone #F2EEE4 versus P2 linen #F3F0E7, plus P2's second ground #FAF8F3 for plate interiors, which P1 does not have. Settle to one ground plus an optional plate step. The 22px faint graticule is shared and should stay shared.

5. MOTION VERBS. P1 ships SETTLE and SWEEP. P2 ships SETTLE (inherited verbatim), TRAVERSE, PLUMB, RECLASSIFY and SHUFFLE — and deliberately omits SWEEP, because P2 forbids animated line-drawing across a seam and SWEEP is exactly the gesture that would invite one. The review must decide whether SWEEP survives repo-wide with a 'never across a seam' constraint, or becomes P1-local.

6. TYPEFACE COUNT. P1 runs two families (Newsreader, Martian Mono). P2 runs four, adding IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono for on-chart annotation and dense tabular numerals. The review should decide whether Plex enters the repo system as the label/data superfamily — which I would argue for, since any project with a dense matrix will need it — or stays P2-local, in which case P2 should justify the extra two font loads on its own.

One thing that does NOT need reconciling and should be noted as evidence the system is holding: --ink #15181D, the 22px graticule, SETTLE, the light-mode-only stance, and Martian Mono as the hero numeral face all carry over unchanged. The repo already has a shared substrate; the argument is only about what sits on top of it.

proposals.name: THE CHAIN OF CUSTODY
proposals.one_line: Every number in this project is testimony taken by a named institution with an interest; the design draws whose hands it passed through, and treats a break in the chain as the story rather than as a caveat.
proposals.philosophy:
The brief's risk is real: "institutions are the protagonists" usually degrades into an illustrated lecture, because institutions are nouns and charts want verbs. The escape is to notice something true about this specific data layer — uncertainty here is not noise, it is a fingerprint of the same power the essay is about.

Look at why the frozen numbers are weak where they are weak. The 1914 CI is $990m–$1.45bn because no institution existed yet to count. Era 5's money-type split is eight grade-C claims because no compiler ever published it. The click-fraud rate is 3–20% because the only party holding the log was the defendant. There is no free by-medium series for 2011–2025 because MAGNA licenses its series — counting became private property. Coen's 89-year series ends at 2007 because an agency holding company shut it down. Every hole and every wide interval in `adspend.json` was produced by an act of an institution named in the narrative.

So: make custody the primary visual axis, and the rigor layer and the thesis become the same object. The 80% CI stops being a caveat drawn next to the argument and becomes the argument's principal evidence.

Three cognitive commitments follow.

First, **spend the hue budget on one semantic axis and nothing else.** Ware and Brewer both put usable categorical hue at 6–8 and preattentive pop-out at 4–5; thread 1's seven funder classes sit at that ceiling. Rather than burn colour on media, money-types and compilers — which is what every ad-history chart does — I collapse the funders into a single *ordinal* diverging ramp (the seller's own hand → an adversary's hand) and give everything else material and position. An ordinal luminance-and-hue ramp is read as an order preattentively; seven arbitrary categories are not. Media identity then rides on texture, which Gestalt similarity grouping handles as strongly as hue, and which has the decisive side benefit described in P1 below: two different materials cannot be read as one continuous line.

Second, **encode uncertainty at rest, not in motion.** Cleveland & McGill rank position-on-a-common-scale first and length second; motion amplitude is not on the list, because two amplitudes cannot be compared accurately. P1 could afford ambient jitter because uncertainty was the emotional payload and the substrate was a particle field. P2's substrate is 30,000 words of readability-gated prose with named actors as figures; ambient motion there is an involuntary attention capture (Bartram, Ware) competing with reading. So uncertainty becomes a static glyph whose *length* is the interval — and motion is demoted to an event verb that fires only when the custody of a number changes.

Third, **make the honest drawing the only drawable one.** 65 claims must never be points; three era-7 pools must never be sorted. Discipline is not a design deliverable — a linter is. The frozen data already carries `unranked_pairs`, `ci80`, `grade` and `taxonomy_seam`; the build reads those and fails on violation. Norman's forcing functions applied to a chart pipeline.

The result is a site whose colour, whose glyph, whose progress bar and whose failure modes all say the same sentence: somebody counted this, and somebody paid them to.
proposals.why_this_project:
Three properties of *this* material, not institutional history in general, select this direction.

**1. The dataset is autobiographical.** `adspend.json` is not neutral evidence about the advertising market; it is an artefact of it. Its eight series were compiled by an agency holding company (Coen/McCann), a media-buying arm of the same holding company (MAGNA), the sellers' own trade body (IAB/PwC), the tax authority, the publishers' association (NAA), and the Census. Its 19 concordance entries are institutional decisions: Coen renamed Billboards to Out of Home at 2.77× on identical 1999 data; Yellow Pages simply appears in 1980 with no restatement; the internet line is 49.7% of the IAB's by 2007 because the compiler's own curator says it undercounts. A direction that treats the data layer as a lens onto the story wastes the fact that the data layer *is* the story. Custody makes the seams first-class content, which the freeze explicitly demands ("seams are content and must be visible").

**2. All four chosen threads are custody questions with different objects.** Who counted (thread 1) is custody of the measurement. Who took a cut (thread 2) is custody of the dollar. Who was allowed in (thread 3) is custody of the door on the buy side. Who owns the front door (thread 4) is custody of the door on the supply side. One grammar covers four chapters, so the reader learns the vocabulary once and spends the remaining three chapters on content rather than on decoding a new chart form. That is a large working-memory dividend across a long read.

**3. The two natural experiments are custody experiments.** 1987 people meters and the 2021 Nielsen undercount are the strongest evidence in the whole record precisely because the instrument changed and the world did not. Those are not illustrations of a thesis; they are the controlled trials. A design whose signature interaction is a two-position instrument switch puts the reader's hand on the very mechanism the evidence turns on. The 2000 taxonomy seam (P4) has the identical logical shape — change the classifier, the number moves, nothing about the market moved — and so does the ranking-rule switch in the simulator, except there the allocation genuinely changes, which is the one case that proves the reader was right to expect otherwise.

Against the illustrated-lecture risk specifically, five load-bearing hooks: every thread visual is generated from claim records rather than hand-authored annotation, so a mis-sourced claim visibly changes the picture; each mark's custody hue is derived from that claim's own `sources` field; two of the four threads argue from interval *width* rather than centrals (era 5's bracket narrowing 12.2pp → 7.70pp with its floor pinned at 20.8; era 7's overlap wash); the signature interaction is a data operation over frozen claims, not a narration; and the build fails on a wide-CI point or a sorted unranked pair.

hard_problems.solution:
A three-register chart system on one shared 1840–2026 x-axis, called THE DOCKET, governed by one rule: ONE COMPILER, ONE MATERIAL.

Register A (top, always visible) — THE COMPILERS' RAILS. Not money: counting. One horizontal bar per compiler showing its coverage, basis and access, coloured on the custody ramp: coen_mce 1919–2007 (agency-compiled, billings, free, DEAD), magna 1980–2025 (media-buying arm, media-owner revenue, LICENSED — drawn hatched where unreadable), iab_pwc 1996–2025 (sellers report on themselves — deep amber), irs_soi 1960–2022 (cross-check only, dashed), naa_newspaper 1950–2010, census_manufactures 1909–1937, benchmarks_pre1919 1867–1918, bridge_mce_mg8 1980–2007 (ours, ghost material). The reader sees the Coen rail stop at 2007 before any line stops at 2007.

Register B (middle) — THE MONEY, in two modes. Default is THE STRIP BOARD: one thin panel per medium, each with its own flat zero baseline, vertically aligned on the shared x-axis, 10 curated media by default and all 27 labels on expand. Never a stacked area or streamgraph. Total mode is TWO RIBBONS: across 1980–2007 Coen and MAGNA are both drawn, in their own materials, and the vertical distance between them is rendered as an explicit measured object — THE WEDGE — carrying its own label and its own decomposition on hover (raw break −23.43% at 1980; like-for-like wedge −7.21%; scope share 69.2%). The bridge series is a third material: hatched ghost rail, grade-C texture, CI envelope permanently on, legend entry reading 'our construction.'

Register C (bottom) — THE SEAM STRIP. A tick at each of the 19 concordance entries, each tick raising a seam card with the magnitude numbers already in the data: 1935 (partition begins; 'other' is 62.6% of 1919), 1980 (Yellow Pages enters at $2,900m as miscellaneous drops $2,074m), 1990 (Television splits), 1999/2000 (Billboards → Out of Home, 2.771×), 2004+ (Coen internet falls to 49.7% of IAB by 2007, a $10,677m gap), 2007 (series ends), 2011–2025 (no free by-medium series). Seam ticks extend as hard vertical rules through Register B.

The 2011–2025 by-medium hole is drawn as a hole: bare Foolscap under a hatched ceiling, one label, zero interpolation, forever.

Post-2015 Magna-vs-IRS divergence of roughly a third is drawn as a second permanent wedge, so no single US ad-spend number ever appears without its rail named.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Readers integrate a stacked area by good continuation, which is exactly why silent splices work — continuation is preserved across the join, so the eye manufactures a trend. Two defences. First, material difference defeats similarity grouping: a drawn line and a hatched ribbon cannot be perceptually chained, so the 2007/2008 break is refused at the level of perception rather than at the level of a footnote. Second, the seam ticks impose uniform connectedness (Palmer & Rock), which dominates good continuation in the Gestalt hierarchy — bounded regions read as separate objects even when adjacent.

The strip board replaces stacked area because middle bands in a stack require length judgements against a non-flat baseline, which Cleveland & McGill place near the bottom of the accuracy ranking; aligned panels with individual zero baselines convert every trajectory into position-on-a-common-scale, the top-ranked judgement, and preserve cross-medium comparison through common alignment rather than through summed length. data-to-viz's stacked-area caveat is thereby satisfied by construction rather than by care.

Register A exists to set expectation before violation. A seam that arrives unannounced is a surprise the reader resolves as data; a seam the reader was told to expect two registers earlier is resolved as method. The wedge is drawn as an object rather than as whitespace because Tufte's data-ink argument cuts both ways — the most important quantity on that screen is the difference between two rulers, and unlabelled whitespace encodes nothing.

hard_problems.solution:
Two moves, and neither of them distorts the axis.

Move 1 — BENCHMARK STONES. Time stays strictly linear (a compressed or broken time axis for the sparse era would be a documented deception). What changes is the mark. 1867, 1880, 1900, 1914 and 1918 are drawn as heavy rectangles, not points and not a line: rectangle height is the 80% CI on the dollar axis ($50m over $30–80m; $200m over $140–280m; $1.2bn over $990m–$1.45bn), rectangle width is the year's own softness, since these were estimated decades after the fact and two credible lineages disagree by 13–19%. The Printers'-Ink/T444 lineage and Coen's 1999 revision are drawn as two offset stones per year, not averaged. Between the stones: bare paper. Seventy-seven years of emptiness is the content, and it is labelled once: 'Nobody was keeping an annual count.'

Move 2 — ERA 1 RUNS ON THE INSTITUTIONAL LANE. Since quantity is absent, era 1's chapter is carried by the entity lifelines that carry every other chapter: Palmer 1841 (paid by publishers, ~25%), Rowell's directory 1869, Ayer's open contract 1875 (the agent flips to the buyer's side), commission settles at 15% early 1890s, 1893 publishers refuse commission to direct buyers, ABC founded 1914. The reader experiences era 1 at full narrative density and honest quantitative sparsity, because the site's protagonists are institutions and institutions are continuously present here even though money is not.

The hinge is 1914, and the design makes it the most instrumented vertical in the first half of the site: ABC founded, $1.2bn benchmark, 22,754 publications, advertising 64.9% of newspaper income, classified ~13% of newspaper receipts on an 8–22% range. Then the CI envelope visibly narrows as the reader scrolls past 1914 into 1919 and again at 1935. The uncertainty band's own width tells thread 1's story without a word: the intervals tighten when somebody starts counting.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
The perceptual honesty rule for missing data is that absence must be encoded as absence — any interpolation across 1840–1918 would be read as measurement, because a line's whole job is to assert continuity between its endpoints. But absence is also an engagement problem, and the wrong fix is to fake density. The right fix is to change channel: the reader's working memory is not idle across era 1, it is tracking six named actors instead of a curve, which is well inside the 4±1 chunk budget and is exactly the load this direction wants to train.

Drawing a benchmark as a rectangle rather than a point uses the length channel for the interval and refuses the point channel entirely, which is the same grammar as P3 and means era 1 needs no special-case explanation. Offsetting the two vintages rather than averaging them keeps a disagreement visible as a disagreement — averaging would convert a fact about compilers into a false precision about the 1920s.

The narrowing envelope at 1914 is the strongest single piece of evidence-as-argument in the essay: it is a purely perceptual demonstration of the thread-1 claim, delivered before the claim is made, and therefore read as observation rather than as persuasion.

hard_problems.solution:
I replace measurement jitter with THE CUSTODY MARK — one composite glyph used everywhere a number appears: in charts, inline in prose, in tooltips, in the docket sheet, in the simulator. Rendered at three sizes (inline 14px, chart 20px, hero 48px).

Anatomy. (1) THE SPAN: a horizontal bar whose length is the 80% CI on the local scale. (2) THE CENTRAL TICK: a vertical tick at the central value. (3) THE CUSTODY NOTCH: a small notch whose vertical offset from the span encodes who counted — above = an interested hand, on = arm's length, below = an adversary — redundantly coloured on the amber↔cyan ramp, so the encoding survives protanopia and greyscale via position. (4) THE GRADE TEXTURE: A = solid span, square end-caps; B = solid span, open end-caps; C = dashed span with feathered ends, because the tails are ours. Grade is texture, not colour, so it never competes with custody hue.

The hard rule: the 65 claims whose CI exceeds 60% of their central are drawn with NO CENTRAL TICK. Span only. Removing the tick is the strongest available statement — there is no point estimate to anchor on. A build-time linter reads `ci80` and `central` from the frozen files and fails the build if any claim with ratio > 0.6 is bound to a point mark, anywhere, in any chart.

Prose parity: because the readability gates already force the prose to state ranges in words, the inline custody mark sits beside the sentence's number and matches it exactly. The reader never has to hold 'grade C, wide range' in working memory across a scroll.

Motion is not deleted, it is demoted. SWAY — a single damped oscillation, two cycles, 900ms, amplitude proportional to CI width — fires only on first reveal of a wide-CI mark and at the instrument switches. At most one SWAY per viewport per scroll stop. Jitter becomes an event, not a state.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Cleveland & McGill's ranking puts position-on-a-common-scale first and length second; motion amplitude is not on the ranking at all, because observers cannot accurately compare two oscillation amplitudes. P1's jitter was correct for P1: uncertainty was the subject, the marks were a particle field, and the payload was affective. P2 inverts every one of those conditions. Uncertainty here is evidence in an argument about institutions, the substrate is prose with named actors as figures, and the reader must compare intervals — era 5's 12.2pp against 7.70pp, era 7's three overlapping pools — which motion cannot support and length can.

There is also an attention cost. Motion is the most powerful preattentive channel and is involuntary (Bartram, Ware): 65 shimmering marks on a reading page continuously steal fixations from the protagonists. Demoting motion to a transient keeps its informativeness ('this number is loose') and removes its ambient tax. It also removes a real battery and reduced-motion liability across 505 claims on mobile.

Dropping the central tick for the 65 widest claims is an anti-anchoring device in Kahneman's precise sense: a visible point estimate is an anchor even when the text disclaims it, and the only reliable fix is to not draw one. Splitting grade onto texture and custody onto hue keeps the two rigor dimensions on separable channels rather than on one integral one — an essential condition for reading either dimension independently.

hard_problems.solution:
THE RECLASSIFICATION — one block of money, two ledgers.

Era 5's 2000 market is drawn as unit blocks: one block = $1B of the $247.5bn Coen total, so ~247 objects, well inside a countable-at-a-glance field. Four bins: national brand, local retail, classified, direct response. The local Yellow Pages block — $11,135m, 4.4995 points of the 2000 market — is a contiguous, distinctly-edged group of 11 blocks with its own outline. It is THE SAME ELEVEN OBJECTS in both views.

A two-position switch, labelled in gate-passing plain language: 'Split the phone book by who bought it' / 'Put all phone-book money in one pool.' Flipping it moves those 11 objects, and only those 11, from local_retail to direct_response along a visible arc (REASSIGN, 640ms). The other 236 blocks are nailed down: identical positions, identical count, zero motion. No block is created. No block is destroyed.

Layer two, and this is the part that outruns a normal seam treatment. Above each bin sits its 80% CI bracket, and the brackets do not simply translate with the centrals. Local retail goes 28.32% → 23.82%, but its interval NARROWS from 12.2pp to 7.70pp while its floor holds at 20.8. Annotation, gate-passing: 'The floor did not move. Four and a half of the seven and a half points of doubt WERE this rule. Settle the rule and that doubt goes away. The rest is real disagreement.'

Layer three, mandatory and always on: THE OVERLAP BAR. Beneath the bins, local retail's and direct response's intervals are drawn as two spans on one axis, with the region where they overlap rendered as a solid hatched block labelled 'These two cannot be ranked. That is true under both rules.' The overlap never blinks during the switch. Whichever way the reader leaves the scene, they cannot leave with 'direct response was bigger.'

The scene's caption, which is also its thesis: 'Two rules. One block of money. The order flips. Both rules are fair. Nothing about the market changed.'

A site-wide corollary: every cross-era chart uses `by_money_type_alt` (unified-intent), and any chart that touches era 5's geographic split beside another era fails the build, per the freeze's cross_era_comparable_basis field.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Change blindness works for us here if and only if exactly one thing moves. Rensink's result is that observers miss changes across a transition when many elements change at once; the inverse is that a single moving set in an otherwise frozen field is captured involuntarily. Freezing 236 blocks and moving 11 makes the mechanism the only signal on screen.

Object constancy does the argumentative work. Because the blocks retain identity, the reader perceives REASSIGNMENT, not growth — growth would require new objects to appear, and none do. 'The flip is an artifact of classification, not a fact about the market' is thereby encoded as object permanence rather than asserted as a caption. This is precisely the user's standing preference put to analytical use: the morph teaches the transformation instead of swapping one chart for another.

The bracket layer matters because it separates two things readers routinely conflate: reducing a *convention* is not the same as learning something about the world. A narrowing interval with a pinned floor is the visible signature of that distinction, and it is in the frozen data rather than invented for the scene.

The persistent overlap bar is an anti-framing device. Under a two-state toggle, whichever state the reader last saw becomes the remembered fact (recency plus framing). An invariant that survives both states is the only reliable takeaway from a toggle, so the invariant is drawn continuously and the varying part is drawn as the thing that moves.

hard_problems.solution:
THE UNRANKED FIELD. Four spans on one shared dollar axis, deliberately unsorted, with the unrankedness drawn rather than captioned.

Geometry. Four horizontal spans on a common $-axis: national brand $146B [100, 187], local retail $94B [60, 123], direct response $151B [117, 187], classified $10B. Position-on-a-common-scale is the most accurate available judgement and it is honest here because the axis is the quantity itself. The spans are NOT sorted by central. They are ordered by the sequence the essay met them, and the axis label says so: 'ordered as this essay met them, not by size.'

The three unranked pools carry NO CENTRAL MARK — span only. Classified, which the record does rank ('its interval [7.9, 10.1] does not touch any other pool's'), keeps its central tick. The visual difference between 'has a tick' and 'has no tick' then reads directly as 'we know where this one sits / we know only roughly where these sit.'

THE OVERLAP WASH: a translucent vertical band across $117B–$123B, the range where all three big spans coexist, labelled 'Any of these three could be the largest.'

THE PROOF, on tap: hovering or tapping any span raises the three estimating methods behind it, shown as three small ranked triplets that visibly disagree about which pool is biggest. Unrankedness is demonstrated by exhibiting the disagreement, not asserted by a disclaimer.

THE OVERSHOOT: the four pools sum to 100.6%. The axis extends past the total and a small tail block is drawn, labelled 'Our four pools add to 100.6%. We show the overshoot rather than shave it.'

Enforcement. The frozen `unranked_pairs` array is read at build time. Any chart binding two or more claims from a declared unranked pair into a stack, a sorted bar, a ranked list, a pie or a treemap fails the build. Era 1's 1914 row inherits the same treatment automatically: four rough sizes summing to 62%, with the 38% residual drawn as its own labelled void block, and the single safe statement — 'classified was the smallest' — as the only ordering the scene asserts.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
A stack, a bar chart and a ranked list all impose a total order through position, and position is the channel readers trust most. Using the most trusted channel to assert an ordering the evidence refuses is the worst available error, and no caption repairs it — the graphic wins. So the design gives up the ordering and keeps the axis: spans on a shared quantitative scale communicate magnitude at rank-1 accuracy while communicating nothing about rank between overlapping pools.

Withdrawing the central tick for exactly the unranked pools is a differential anchoring defence. If all four carried ticks, readers would order the ticks, because points on a line are ordered by construction; leaving one pool with a tick and three without makes the absence itself informative and gives the reader a within-scene contrast to learn from.

The overlap wash exploits Gestalt common region: a bounded translucent area binds the three spans into one group whose internal order is not specified, which is the exact proposition the data supports. And showing three disagreeing methods converts an epistemic claim into an observation — readers accept 'these experts disagree' far more readily than 'this cannot be known,' and here the former is literally true.

The linter is the load-bearing part. Ordering discipline degrades under deadline; a forcing function does not.

hard_problems.solution:
THE BENCH — the reader sits where Google sat. One persistent stage, three fixed zones, all visible at once. No tabs: tabs hide state and impose recall cost, and this simulator's whole lesson is that state you cannot see is the state that prices you.

THE SLATE (left): the cast as persistent characters — Aster, Brindle, Cedar — each a card with bid, predicted CTR and true CTR held visibly apart. The same three advertisers travel through all ten auction scenarios, so the reader learns transformations rather than reading ten charts. Every card is stamped 'invented cast — no calibration' on ghost material, because none of these numbers is an empirical claim.

THE PAGE (centre): a mock results page with two slots. Allocation is physical — ads move between slots. The unit is one click = one particle, so sc-01's 18 clicks against sc-02's 58 is a countable object difference, not a bar length.

THE TILL (right): two counters on separate axes that never merge — total money collected, and average price per click. Different units, never one chart.

The guided rail: 21 scenarios as a horizontal dock of numbered stops in two named chunks, YIELD (sc-01…sc-10) and VOLUME (D1…D11), current stop highlighted, all reachable. Scroll drives it downward; the dock allows return. Twenty-one undifferentiated buttons is a 21-way Hick's-law choice; a rail with a current position is a 2-way choice plus optional jump, and two chunks of ten sit inside a chunked working-memory budget.

Required teaching, in order. sc-01: the AdRank column reads 0.03 / 0.04 / 0.05 — the bid order is the exact reverse of the expected-revenue order. sc-02: THE SIGN FLIP (the essay's signature; see signature_interaction). sc-03: bid-minus-price annotated per winner, and the pay-your-bid row rendered on GHOST MATERIAL — the same hatched stock as constructed data — so a counterfactual can never be mistaken for a measurement. sc-04: the reader is handed the BIDDER's seat and drags Vale's bid from 10 down through 5, watching Vale's own payoff ($400 → $640) on the bidder card, not the till; a persistent chip reads 'YOU ARE: one bidder.' sc-05: a three-position toggle (naive truthful $760 / one shader $660 / lowest envy-free $440), and from this point onward EVERY revenue figure anywhere in the simulator carries the toggle position as an attached chip, and the till bar is drawn INSIDE a translucent $440–$760 band, so the number is seen as a position in a band rather than as a fact. sc-06: two bars that start level at the (n−1)/n equilibrium shading before the reader breaks it, with the frozen-bid trap shown as an 86% apparent windfall on ghost material, and a pinned caption: 'This was DISPLAY. Search never went first price.' sc-07: one slider on Cedar's TRUE ctr with predicted pinned at 5% and drawn in deep amber (the interested hand) while true is drawn as a void outline (nobody outside could observe it); break-even marked at 1.99% on the slider track. sc-08: one bidder, one ad, an EMPTY CHAIR where the price-setting rival should sit, and reserve $0.01 → $1.00 producing 100× revenue. sc-09: three knobs on the ex-1 cast under a permanent banner — 'The ad copy, the cast and the query never change while these move' — with gamma's slider carrying a void-textured assumption label reading 'this exponent has never been disclosed.' sc-10: two panels, opposite directions, same year.

THE DOOR (the distribution engine, D1–D11) is a separate stage with a separate material, because filed dollars must never share an axis with the invented cast. Filed dollars are solid, square-capped grade-A spans on a $-axis. The two stages co-occur only in D5 (yield sets the distribution budget), separated by a labelled divider with two independent axes. Highlights surfaced: D1's exposure curve max(0, G − sR) with the filed 2002 and 2003 points marked on the axis; D3's equity leg as two spans 82× apart on one log-$ axis, labelled 'The cheap leg was the expensive one'; D4's 95.5¢ against 21.3¢; D8's composition inversion, with network share always carrying its basis (31.9% of growth / 30.8% of total revenue / 9.4% net of TAC); and D9's liquidity externality as an OPEN-QUESTION SWITCH which, when turned on, fills its own region with void texture and the label 'Nobody has ever measured this.'

The take-rate control is never a lever. It renders as an outcome readout with the note 'this is what competition did: 9% in 2002, 24.7% in 2006, back to 21.3% in 2008.'
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
The centrepiece has no template, so its structure has to come from the learning literature rather than from a chart taxonomy. Three principles do the work.

Mayer's spatial and temporal contiguity: cause and effect must be adjacent in space and simultaneous in time. That is why allocation, price and revenue are three fixed zones on one stage rather than three tabs — the reader must see the ranking change and the two counters move in the same fixation window, or the sign reversal simply does not land.

Segmenting and pre-training: 21 scenarios delivered as a user-paced rail with named chunks, each teaching one delta from the previous state, is the segmenting principle exactly. And because the cast is constant, the reader has pre-trained on Aster/Brindle/Cedar by scenario three and can spend all capacity on the mechanism.

Seat labelling addresses a specific confusion this material invites: sc-04 is the only scenario where the reader's interest opposes the seller's, and readers who do not notice the switch conclude that shading helps Google. Making the seat a visible, persistent state variable is Norman's visibility-of-system-state applied to point of view.

The material rule earns its keep hardest here. Counterfactual revenue, invented casts, undisclosed parameters and unmeasured effects are four different kinds of not-a-fact, and each of them is the standard way this story gets told wrongly. Rendering all four in the same non-measurement material means a reader who learns one learns all four, and a builder cannot accidentally promote a counterfactual to a finding.

Finally, the persistent band around the till number is the only honest way to display GSP revenue. A number with an error bar reads as a measurement with noise; a number drawn as a position inside a labelled band reads as a choice inside a range, which is what a 1.727× equilibrium band actually is.

hard_problems.solution:
Two components, one data structure.

(a) THE DOCKET SHEET — the per-era scaffold. Every era chapter opens with the same fixed 3×3 card, and the nine cells never change screen position across seven eras:

  CREATORS   BUYERS     SELLERS
  MEDIUM     PRICING    MEASUREMENT
  SCALE      TARGETING  EVENTS

Row 1 is the people, row 2 the machinery, row 3 the magnitude and the shocks. PRICING sits dead centre because the eras are named for it. MEASUREMENT sits immediately right of PRICING because measurement creates pricing, and adjacency encodes that causal claim through proximity. (Eight schema fields plus top-level `events` fills the ninth cell; eras 5–7 additionally carry `unit_economics`, which docks as a footer chip below the grid rather than breaking it — the exception is visibly an exception.)

Each cell holds: field name, a one-line gate-passing answer, the headline number with its custody mark, and a custody wash across the cell where that field has a custodian. Flipping through seven docket sheets, the reader watches the wash migrate from cyan to amber. Thread 1 is thereby delivered passively, seven times, before its chapter ever argues it.

(b) THE COMPARATOR — the answer to 'era 3's PRICING against era 6's without scrolling twice.' Click or tap any cell to PIN it, and the 3×3 transposes into a single 7-row column: that field for all seven eras, each row carrying era name, headline number and custody mark. The 56 cells exist once in the DOM and animate between grid layout and column layout on a D3 join keyed by (era, field). The era you were reading holds position while its eight siblings fly out and six other eras' PRICING cells fly in — the transition teaches the transpose, so the control needs no explanation.

Column mode is where field-level uncertainty becomes visible: era 3's PRICING carries grade-C station-rep rates while era 6's carries grade-A filings, and the grade textures stack into a vertical column showing at a glance which eras we actually know. Same for MEASUREMENT, where the custody notches form a descending staircase from arm's length to the seller's own hand.

Underneath, the component is a real HTML table with proper row and column headers, so screen readers get the full 7×9 matrix regardless of layout mode.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Fixed spatial mapping is the cheapest comprehension subsidy available in a long repeating structure. Holding each field in an invariant screen position across seven repetitions converts a semantic lookup ('where do they discuss pricing?') into a spatial one ('middle centre'), and spatial memory for a small grid is durable and near-free (Ware). By era 4 the reader navigates by muscle memory, which is capacity returned to the content.

The pivot solves the 56-cell problem the way small-multiple transposes always have: a matrix affords two readings, along rows and along columns, and forcing the reader to reconstruct the column reading from seven scattered rows imposes exactly the split-attention cost Mayer warns about. Animating the transpose rather than cutting to it preserves object constancy at the level of information architecture — the cell the reader cares about is trackable through the change, so the reader knows what happened rather than inferring it from a new screen.

Custody wash on the cells is a small multiple of a heatmap in disguise. Seven low-resolution colour fields, seen in sequence, produce a trend perception that no single chart of the same data would produce as cheaply, and it primes the thread-1 chapter so that chapter reads as confirmation rather than as assertion.

hard_problems.solution:
Four rules, then the specifics.

RULE 1: DROP INTERACTIONS, NEVER EVIDENCE. RULE 2: ONE REGISTER AT A TIME. RULE 3: HOVER BECOMES TAP-TO-PIN, with a persistent card, one pin at a time. RULE 4: CONTINUOUS CONTROLS BECOME DISCRETE MARKED STOPS.

THE DOCKET ROTATES. On desktop, three stacked registers on a horizontal 1840–2026 axis. On mobile the time axis rotates to VERTICAL and time runs down the screen, because at 390px a 180-year horizontal axis gives 2.2px per year and every era becomes illegible, while 180 years down roughly six screens gives comfortable density and makes the scroll gesture itself the pan. Compilers' rails move to the left gutter as vertical bars; the money becomes horizontal extent; seam ticks become full-width horizontal rules with their cards inline in the scroll. This is a re-encoding to fit the device's dominant gesture, not a degradation.

THE STRIP BOARD REDUCES. Ten aligned sparklines at 390px sit below the threshold for reading shape, so mobile ships four named panels plus a chip row that lets the reader swap in any two media to compare. Two aligned panels is the comparison mobile can actually support.

THE BENCH, REDUCED. Same three zones, stacked vertically, stepped rather than free-form. Every continuous slider becomes 3–5 marked stops, using the stops the frozen data already specifies: gamma at 1.0 / 0.9503 / 0.5 / 0.0, format multiplier at 1.0 / 1.075 / 1.2423. sc-04's continuous bid drag becomes a stepped bid ladder (10 / 8 / 6.5 / 5) with the payoff readout pinned directly above the thumb, satisfying contiguity on a small screen. One live control per scenario — the one that carries the lesson.

DELIBERATELY DROPPED ON MOBILE, and stated in the UI rather than hidden: (1) free-form multi-parameter exploration — you cannot set bids and CTRs and reserve simultaneously; (2) the full 27-medium strip board; (3) point-level hover inspection in the money register, replaced by one-at-a-time tap-to-pin; (4) sc-10's side-by-side two-panel comparison, which becomes a swipe between two states with a difference readout, because two panels at 190px each are unreadable; (5) the entity-lifeline field's full 180-year span at once — mobile shows one era's slice with entities entering and exiting at its boundaries; (6) the docket sheet's 3×3 grid, which becomes a 1×9 vertical list in the same fixed order, with the pivot preserved because the pivot is the thing mobile needs most.

NEVER DROPPED ON MOBILE: every custody mark, every CI span, every grade texture, every seam card, every unranked verdict, every void texture, the bidder-mode chip, and the 'YOU ARE' seat label. If something must go it is an interaction, not a caveat.

Performance: Canvas for the 247-block reclassification and the click particles, SVG for everything else; particle counts capped at 250 (already true of every scene); custody marks batch into an instanced sprite sheet on Canvas above 200 marks in view.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
The axis rotation is the one decision that makes this responsive case tractable, and it is a perceptual argument rather than a layout convenience. Reading a trend requires a legible aspect ratio; 180 years across 390px compresses each era to about 25px, below the width at which a shape can be judged at all. Rotating aligns the data's dominant dimension with the device's dominant gesture, so panning costs nothing and no zoom control is needed — and zoom controls are where mobile data journalism usually dies.

Stepped controls follow from Fitts's law and from the fact that a fingertip occludes roughly 10mm of the screen it is manipulating. A continuous slider requires simultaneously fine motor control and observation of a distant readout; marked stops require a single tap and let the reader observe the SETTLE with their hand out of the way. The stops are not an approximation of the desktop experience, because the frozen data already declares the pedagogically meaningful values — the desktop's continuity is the luxury, not the lesson.

The rule that caveats never get cut inverts the usual responsive hierarchy, where nuance is the first thing dropped. In a project whose thesis is that measurement discipline decays under commercial pressure, shipping a mobile edition with the error bars removed would be a self-refutation.

hard_problems.solution:
One form reused four times, THE LIFELINE FIELD, with a genuinely different operation per thread so it does not become monotonous. Thread 1's two-track timeline is accepted in spirit and upgraded topologically.

THREAD 1 — WHO COUNTED, AND WHO PAID THE COUNTER. Two tied tracks. Top: counting institutions as lifelines with birth and death — Rowell's directory 1869, ABC 1914 (tripartite-funded, the world's first third-party media audit), CAB 1930–1946 (advertiser-funded at $70/month, $33,045 in year one, dies when the funders change), Hooper 1934 (funded by magazine publishers who thought radio was overstated, running ~20% above CAB), Nielsen buys Hooper 1950, Broadcast Rating Council 1964, DART 1996, the seller's own log 2002, the MRC pulling Nielsen's accreditation 2021. Bottom: the FUNDER, drawn as a lifeline directly beneath, coloured on the custody ramp. The tie between them is a vertical connector carrying the ramp value.

The upgrade: THE TIE GOES SLACK, THEN THE LINES MERGE. Where counter and seller become the same entity, from about 1996, the two tracks converge into a single double-width lifeline in deepest amber. 'The seller became the auditor' is then topological rather than annotated — a reader who takes nothing else away takes away that two lines became one line.

The two price shocks are the site's signature interaction instantiated: 1987 people meters (measured prime-time audience −10% overnight, CBS −13%, ABC −13%, make-goods owed in scatter worth more than the upfront sold) and 2021 Nielsen (a 2–6% undercount the VAB valued at ≥$468M). Both are the same two-position instrument switch, thirty-four years apart, and the repetition is the argument.

THREAD 2 — THE INTERMEDIARY'S CUT. Form: THE DOLLAR'S JOURNEY, seven times. Not a stacked bar — the denominators differ per era, so stacking would assert a comparability the evidence forbids. One dollar as 100 blocks walked down a corridor of hands, once per era, as separated small multiples each carrying its own denominator in words. Era 1: 15 to the agency, 85 to the publisher. Era 2: 15 agency, 62 network, 23 stations. Era 4: the Economic Census run — commissions actually received at 14.13 / 13.92 / 14.16 / 13.18%, then 10.98% in 1997, which contradicts the received story that the commission died in the 1980s. Era 6: 9% → 24.7% → 21.3% on syndicated inventory. Era 7: THE CORRIDOR CANNOT BE CLOSED — 51 blocks reach the publisher, 15 blocks fall into a void-textured block labelled 'nobody can say,' and the ANA figure (~36¢ of a DSP dollar reaches a consumer) sits beside it as a second corridor behind a labelled 'different ruler' divider. The 100 blocks are the same 100 objects across all seven corridors. Final image: seven corridors, and the only one with a hole in it is the most-measured era.

THREAD 3 — WHO WAS ALLOWED TO BUY. Form: TWO PANELS THAT MUST NOT BE JOINED, with a gate between them. Left panel: classified and directory dollar share, eras 1–4, sitting stubbornly at 3–13% of the market. Right panel: advertiser head count on a log axis — Yahoo 3,800 in 1998, Overture 53,000 then 80,000, Google ~1M drawn as a span with no central tick (CI 550,000–2,600,000), Meta >10M drawn in void outline with a 'the seller says' chip. Between them a labelled gutter: 'These two panels measure different things. Do not read them as one line.' The centrepiece is THE GATE CARD — Overture and AdWords in the same year as two literal doorways with their requirements drawn as bars across each opening: Overture's 10¢ minimum bid, $20 monthly minimum and human editorial review against AdWords' one-off $5 activation, no monthly minimum, automated approval. The reader sets a monthly budget on a stepped control and watches a buyer particle attempt each era's doors, 1840s to now. In every era one door is open — which is the thread's actual finding.

THREAD 4 — THE RENT ON THE FRONT DOOR. Form: ONE INSTRUMENT, SEVEN INSTANCES, TWO ROWS, NO DUAL AXIS. Top row: the payout as a share of the revenue it generated, every panel on an identical 0–100% scale — 27% affiliate compensation in 1938, 5–20% station reps, 56% Overture TAC, ~85% AOL, 36% Safari. Bottom row: the same deals in absolute dollars, every panel on an identical log-$ scale, so 1938 and 2021's $26.3B coexist, with a labelled 'each step is ten times' ruler. Read across the top row: the rate barely moved in eighty years. Read across the bottom: the amount grew by orders of magnitude. Two true statements, two rows, and never the dual axis that would fuse them into a false one. Inset: the AOL warrant, $13.871M carried against ~$1,134.6M realised, two spans 82× apart on one log axis. Closer: the September 2025 remedy drawn as a gate CLOSING on exclusivity while the payment lifeline runs straight through it, unbroken.
hard_problems.cognitive_rationale:
Reusing one form four times is the largest working-memory saving available across four consecutive synthesis chapters. Each new chart form costs a decoding pass before any content is absorbed; a shared grammar means threads 2, 3 and 4 spend their opening seconds on content. The variation comes from the operation performed on the form, not from the form, which keeps novelty without keeping cost.

The merge in thread 1 is the design's single best perceptual argument. Two converging lines becoming one is a figure-ground event that survives skimming, greyscale, thumbnail size and a reader who reads no captions at all — properties no annotation possesses. It also uses the strongest available Gestalt cue, common fate followed by unification, to carry the strongest claim in the record.

Thread 2 refuses stacking for the reason P1 refuses it plus one more: the era stacks are not commensurable, since the denominators are percent of gross billings, percent of net time sales retained, gross margin, percent of network revenue and percent of an end-to-end chain. Separated small multiples with per-panel denominators make the incommensurability structural. The unclosable era-7 corridor is the thread's punchline delivered as a shape.

Thread 3's gutter is a deliberate anti-continuity device. A dollar share and a head count on one axis would be a category error that the eye would nonetheless read as a trend, so uniform connectedness is used to prevent it — the same tool P1 uses on the Coen/MAGNA seam, applied to a units problem rather than a basis problem.

Thread 4's two-row treatment exists because dual axes are the canonical way to manufacture a crossing that is not in the data. Splitting share and level onto two rows with identical within-row scales gives both readings at rank-1 accuracy and gives the false reading at no accuracy, which is the correct allocation.

proposals.type:
Three faces, two of them shared with P1, one deliberately swapped because the protagonist changed.

**Archivo** (variable, Google Fonts) — institutions, headlines, and all in-chart numerals in its tabular lining figures. Institution names are set in Archivo Expanded SemiBold, uppercase, +0.06em tracking, so a name reads like lettering over a door: NIELSEN, THE AUDIT BUREAU OF CIRCULATIONS, OVERTURE, MAGNA. This is the divergence from P1 and it is argued, not aesthetic: P1 made numerals the heroes and chose Martian Mono, a face whose eccentricity is instrumental. In P2 the heroes are named actors and the numbers are evidence about them, so the display face has to carry names beautifully at large sizes and numbers competently at small ones. Archivo does both, has genuine tabular figures, and ships Expanded and Narrow siblings for the docket sheet's tight cells.

**Newsreader** (variable, Google Fonts) — body prose, 19px/1.62 desktop, 17px/1.6 mobile, measure capped at 68 characters. Kept from P1 without change. Non-negotiable given the readability gates: this project is prose-heavy by construction, and a warm reading serif on light ground is the configuration with the best sustained-reading evidence behind it.

**IBM Plex Mono** (Google Fonts) — the rigor chrome and nothing else: CI bounds, A/B/C grades, claim ids, as-of dates, source names, basis labels, the bidder-mode chip. Kept from P1. The rule is strict and it is what makes the rigor layer feel like a layer rather than like decoration: if a piece of text names *where a number came from*, it is Plex Mono at 12–13px in Zinc; if it names *what the number is*, it is Archivo tabular.

Martian Mono is dropped. All three faces subset and preloaded as static WOFF2 on GitHub Pages, with `font-display: optional` on the display face to avoid FOUT on the first screen.
proposals.motion:
Seven named verbs. Two are inherited from P1, five are new, and one P1 device is deliberately retired.

**SETTLE** (inherited) — critically-damped arrival, `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)`. 520ms for layout changes, 720ms for a value arriving at its measured position. Every custody mark arrives with SETTLE.

**SWEEP** (inherited) — near-linear, ~1.6s, for a line drawing left to right across a register. Time is always the swept axis.

**HAND OFF** (new; the site's most-repeated verb) — when a number's custodian changes, the custody notch slides along the ramp and the mark's hue crossfades. 400ms, ease-in-out. Fires at 1914, 1930, 1934, 1950, 1964, 1996, 2002, 2021. It always means exactly one thing: the pen changed hands.

**SWAY** (new; replaces P1's MEASUREMENT JITTER) — a single damped oscillation, two cycles, 900ms, amplitude proportional to the CI width on the local scale. Fires only on first reveal of a wide-CI mark and at the three instrument switches. At most one SWAY per viewport per scroll stop. Motion becomes an event that says 'this number is loose,' never an ambient state.

**REASSIGN** (new) — the P4 verb. The eleven directory blocks travel along a visible arc between bins, 640ms SETTLE, while all 236 other blocks are frozen. The arc persists as a faint trail for 1.2s after arrival, because a motion trail materially aids change detection after the fact.

**PEEL** (new) — thread 2's verb. Blocks detach from the dollar at each hand, staggered 24ms, and SETTLE into the taker's pile.

**CLOSE** (new) — a bar sweeps across an opening, 300ms, linear-out. The only verb that means an institution stopped someone: thread 3's doorways, thread 4's 2025 remedy, the entry gates in the gate card.

Particles snap; they never drift, float or bounce. Scene transitions are scroll-driven and change one thing at a time — highlight or annotate, never both.

**prefers-reduced-motion fallback, complete.** SWAY is replaced by a static hatched CI band at full opacity with a single 120ms fade-in; no oscillation anywhere. HAND OFF becomes an instant hue swap over 120ms with the notch jumping rather than sliding, plus a short static connector drawn between the old and new notch positions so the change is still legible as a change. REASSIGN becomes a crossfade of the eleven blocks out of one bin and into the other, with a permanent static arc drawn between the bins and the count '11' labelled at both ends — the teaching survives without travel. PEEL renders blocks in final position with a 200ms staggered fade and static corridor arrows. SWEEP renders lines complete on entry. SETTLE becomes a 120ms fade with no overshoot and no spring. CLOSE renders the bar already closed with a static motion-arrow glyph. Every scrollytelling scene renders its end state on entry and changes state discretely with no tweening.

Additionally, a persistent in-page motion toggle sits in the site chrome, independent of the OS setting, because a reader may want motion in general and not in a 30,000-word document.
proposals.signature_interaction:
**THE SECOND INSTRUMENT** — a two-position switch that appears four times, with identical mechanics and a different payload each time, and whose fourth appearance breaks its own promise on purpose.

The switch is always the same object: a small two-position toggle labelled with two instrument names, sitting directly beside the number it governs, under a fixed promise printed above it — **"Nothing about the world changes when you flip this."**

**First appearance, thread 1, 1987.** Positions: HOUSEHOLD DIARY / PEOPLE METER. The viewing is the same viewing. Flip it and the measured prime-time network audience drops about 10% overnight; CBS falls 13% and ABC falls 13%, drawn in Redline with hatch and label. Nothing else on screen moves. The reader has just changed the price of American television by touching a switch.

**Second appearance, era 5, the year 2000.** Positions: SPLIT THE PHONE BOOK BY WHO BOUGHT IT / PUT ALL PHONE-BOOK MONEY IN ONE POOL. Eleven blocks move; 236 do not; local retail and direct response swap order; the overlap bar showing that the pair is unranked never blinks.

**Third appearance, thread 1, 2021.** Positions: NIELSEN BEFORE / NIELSEN AFTER. A 2–6% undercount, valued by the VAB at ≥$468M of lost national ad revenue. Same shape, thirty-four years later, and by now the reader recognises the shape before reading the labels.

**Fourth appearance, the simulator, sc-01 → sc-02.** Positions: HIGHEST BID WINS / BID × CLICK RATE WINS. And here the promise is deliberately broken, and the site says so in one line: **"This one really does change something."** The allocation genuinely inverts — Cedar goes to the top, 18 clicks become 58 — and the two counters in the till move in *opposite directions at the same time*: money collected +86.6%, average price per click −42%. Two quantities that every reader expects to move together, visibly separating in a single 720ms SETTLE.

Why this is the one they remember: it is the same gesture four times, so it is learned rather than explained; it is the exact logical shape of the project's two strongest natural experiments; it puts the reader's hand on the instrument rather than on a narration; and its fourth instance is the only place in 180 years where changing the rule changed the world instead of only changing the number. The reader leaves having *performed* the thesis — that in this market, who holds the instrument decides the price — and then having felt the one genuine exception.
proposals.what_it_sacrifices:
**1. The shareable image.** By refusing a single spliced 1919–2026 line, this direction gives up the poster. A splice-and-colour direction gets one screenshot that says "here is 180 years of advertising"; we get a chart system that requires a paragraph. There is no single frame of this site that works as a social card, and that is a real distribution cost.

**2. Time to the headline.** The Instrument gives you a number in the first second. Custody gives you a frame first, and a reader who arrives asking "how big is US advertising?" gets a two-ribbon answer and a question about rulers. Some proportion of readers will read that as evasion and leave.

**3. Colour is spent, so categories are slow.** The entire hue budget goes to the custody axis, which means media, money-types and compilers are encoded by material and position. Material similarity is a learned mapping, not an innate one, so "which line is newspapers?" is measurably slower here than on a colour-coded chart, and it costs the reader roughly one scene of training up front. A direction that colour-codes eight media reads faster on exactly the question most readers arrive with.

**4. Austerity where P1 had warmth.** Retiring ambient jitter is the right analytical call and it is an aesthetic loss. P1's shimmer made uncertainty *felt*; static spans make uncertainty *read*. This site will be calmer, quieter and more document-like, and someone will call it dry. The Instrument's beauty came substantially from that motion and we are not replacing it with anything equally affective.

**5. Twenty-five named actors is over budget.** Making institutions persistent visual entities asks the reader to track roughly two dozen named organisations across 180 years — far past any working-memory limit. It survives only on recognition aids: lifelines, recurring glyphs, the fixed docket sheet. A skimming reader will retain the *shapes* (two lines merged; one corridor has a hole) and almost none of the names. A quantity-first direction would leave a skimmer with three numbers, which is arguably more.

**6. The simulator is a course, not a toy.** Twenty-one scenarios on a guided rail is a ten-to-fifteen minute desktop commitment. A direction that picks the five best scenarios ships something tighter and more likely to be finished. We have chosen completeness over completion rate, and the drop-off between sc-05 and D11 will be steep.

**7. Real build cost.** The material rule, the linter that reads `unranked_pairs` and `ci80`, the pivoting 56-cell docket, the mobile axis rotation and four bespoke thread visuals are all genuine engineering. This direction is plausibly three times the build of a splice-and-colour scrollytell, on a static GitHub Pages target with vanilla JS.

**8. It is weakest where the story is loudest.** The design's honesty devices are most conspicuous exactly at 2011–2025 — the fifteen years readers care most about — because that is where the evidence is thinnest. A reader arriving for "what did Google do to advertising" meets a hatched hole where the by-medium chart should be. That is correct and it is unsatisfying, and no amount of design fixes it, because `ds-gap-001` is a fact about the world.

**Top-left, 48px in from the margin, 40px down.** IBM Plex Mono 12px, uppercase, +0.14em tracking, Zinc: `P2 · THE ATTENTION ECONOMY · 1840s–2026`.

**Left column, x = 48px, width 640px, baseline starting 280px down.** Newsreader Regular 44px/1.18, Graphite:

> **In 1914, someone finally counted the newspapers.**
> **In 2002, the seller started counting itself.**

**40px below that.** Newsreader 20px/1.5, Graphite at 78%:

**Right column, x = 780px, width 612px.** Two custody marks, stacked, 180px apart vertically, each on its own tiny axis. They are the entire teaching payload of the screen.

At the ends, IBM Plex Mono 12px: `550,000` and `2,600,000`. Above it, Archivo SemiBold 30px in Zinc rather than Graphite, because there is no number to state: `— advertisers —`. Beneath, Newsreader 17px: **"Google's advertisers in 2008. The seller never said. We had to estimate."**

Between the two marks, a hairline Zinc bracket connecting them with one IBM Plex Mono 11px label: `94 YEARS`.
